## Contribution Flow - Sessions 1, 2A, 2B, 2C

Implemented shareable contribution links allowing contributors to add voice recordings without authentication.

### Backend Changes

**Database (Session 1)**
- Added `ShareCodeIndex` GSI to DynamoDB for fast code lookups
- Created `backend/src/db/shareCodes.js` with share code CRUD operations
- Schema: 8-character codes with permissions and active status

**API Routes (Session 2A)**
- Created `backend/src/handlers/shareCodeHandler.js` with 4 endpoints:
  - `POST /api/projects/:projectId/share-codes` - Generate share code (authenticated)
  - `GET /api/share-codes/:code/validate` - Validate code (public)
  - `GET /api/projects/:projectId/share-codes` - List codes (authenticated)
  - `DELETE /api/share-codes/:code` - Deactivate code (authenticated)
- Added public endpoints for contributor access:
  - `GET /api/public/photos/:id`
  - `GET /api/public/recordings`
  - `POST /api/public/recordings` (accepts contributorName)

### Frontend Changes

**Contribution Flow (Session 2B)**
- Created `ContributorNamePrompt.tsx` - Captures contributor name on first visit (localStorage)
- Created `ContributePhoto.tsx` - Public page for recording memories
  - Route: `/contribute/:shareCode/photo/:photoId` (no auth required)
  - Validates share code and displays photo
  - Lists existing recordings with playback
  - Inline voice recorder (30-second limit)
  - Mobile-first design with large touch targets
- Added public API functions to `utils/api.ts`

**Host UI (Session 2C)**
- Added share link generation to `ProjectDashboard.tsx`
- Created `ShareLinkModal.tsx` - Copy-to-clipboard modal with QR code
- Share button on each photo for easy link generation

### Key Features
✅ No authentication required for contributors
✅ Share codes with GSI for fast validation
✅ Contributor names stored with recordings
✅ Mobile-optimized recording interface
✅ One-click share link generation for hosts
✅ QR codes for easy mobile sharing

### Testing
Visit `/contribute/:shareCode/photo/:photoId` to test the contribution flow.
Generate share links from the project dashboard "Share" buttons.

commits.messageBody:
Two critical fixes for EC2 video processor auto-stop:

1. IAM Permissions (CRITICAL)
   - Added ec2:StopInstances permission to IAM role
   - Added ec2:DescribeInstances for status checks
   - Scoped to instances with Name tag 'loomed-memories-video-processor'
   - Auto-stop was failing every 5 minutes for 8+ hours due to missing permission

2. Spot Instance Type (one-time → persistent)
   - Changed from 'one-time' to 'persistent' Spot requests
   - Changed InstanceInterruptionBehavior from 'terminate' to 'stop'
   - One-time instances can only be terminated (not stopped/started)
   - Persistent instances can be stopped/started for auto-scaling

Issue Analysis:
- Auto-stop mechanism WAS working correctly
- Detected 5 minutes idle and attempted shutdown
- Failed with: "UnauthorizedOperation: not authorized to perform: ec2:StopInstances"
- Service restarted automatically every 10 seconds (systemd)
- Resulted in infinite retry loop for 8+ hours

Resolution:
- Updated IAM policy with EC2 permissions
- Terminated problematic one-time instance
- Updated launch script for future persistent instances

Next instance will:
- Auto-stop after 5 minutes idle
- Be stoppable/startable manually from console
- Cost ~$0.04/hour only when running

body:
Adds automatic face detection using AWS Rekognition to improve video Ken Burns effects. When photos are uploaded, detected faces are used to calculate a focus point that centers the zoom/pan effect on people.

Architecture:
- S3 trigger fires Lambda on photo uploads (photos/ prefix)
- Lambda calls Rekognition DetectFaces API
- Focus point = centroid of all detected faces
- faceData stored in DynamoDB photo record
- Video generation uses focus point as Ken Burns anchor

S3 Key Format Migration:
- Old: photos/{timestamp}-{filename}
- New: photos/{projectId}/{photoId}/{filename}
- Enables Lambda to parse IDs directly for DynamoDB lookup
- Migration script: npm run migrate-storage
- Backfill script: npm run backfill-faces

Files changed:
- backend/src/faceDetection.js - New Lambda handler
- backend/src/shared/storage.js - New S3 key format
- backend/src/photoHandler.js - Generate photoId early
- backend/src/db/photos.js - generatePhotoId(), updatePhotoFaceData()
- backend/serverless.yml - Lambda + S3 trigger + Rekognition perms
- processing/src/video/effects.py - get_focus_point(), focus_point param
- processing/src/video/models.py - focus_point in PhotoInfo
- processing/src/process_queue.py - Extract faceData from photos

commits.messageBody:
Major refactor replacing the "Groups" concept with "Memories" - a recording
attached to 1-5 photos that plays while those photos display in the video.

Data Model Changes:
- New Memory entity with status (pending/complete), photoIds, recording fields
- Recordings now tied to Memories instead of individual photos
- Photos have inVideo boolean instead of groupId
- Contributors auto-create Memory when recording via share code

New Dashboard Tabs:
- Photo Library: Grid view with filters (All/In Video/Not in Video), bulk actions
- Video Builder: Timeline view with drag-drop reordering, memory detail panel
- Add Photos to Memory modal for expanding memories (up to 5 photos)

Contributor Flows:
- Flow 1: Browse and Record - General share link, pick a photo, record
- Flow 2: Share Specific Photos - Host shares 1-5 photos as pending memory,
  contributor records slideshow with auto-cycling photos (5s each)
- Flow 3: Upload Photo + Record - Contributor uploads, auto-navigates to record

New Components:
- PhotoLibrary.tsx - Photo management with selection and bulk actions
- VideoBuilder.tsx - Timeline editor with dnd-kit drag-drop
- ContributeMemory.tsx - Slideshow recording with volume analysis
- SharePhotosModal.tsx - Create pending memory with share link
- AddPhotosToMemoryModal.tsx - Add photos to existing memory

Volume Analysis Features:
- Post-recording peak/RMS volume calculation
- Volume feedback (good/quiet/loud) with "Use Anyway" option
- Real-time 7-bar equalizer visualization during playback

Migration:
- backend/scripts/migrate-to-memories.js for converting legacy data

Deleted (replaced by Memories):
- Groups: db/groups.js, handlers/groupHandler.js, api/groups.ts
- Pages: GroupDetail.tsx, ContributeGroup.tsx

commits.messageBody:
Phase 2 of photo enhancement pipeline:

**GCS Storage:**
- Photos uploaded to gs://kindred-reels-photos-dev for AI features
- New fields: gcsUri, gcsBucket, gcsPath stored on photo records

**Gemini 3 Flash Analysis:**
- Face detection with bounding boxes (replaces Rekognition DetectFaces)
- Restoration score (0-100) indicating restoration need
- Quality issues detection (faded, scratched, grainy, etc.)
- Orientation detection (0, 90, 180, 270 degrees)
- Estimated decade and color/B&W detection
- Content blocking detection for safety
- Falls back to Rekognition if Gemini fails

**Lambda Package Optimization:**
- Added serverless-esbuild for bundling (260MB → 4.8MB)
- ESM output format for import.meta.url support
- Sharp moved to Lambda Layer
- Simplified deploy scripts (no more sharp:linux swap)

**New Lambda Layer:**
- pillow-heif-gcs-layer:2 with google-cloud-storage + google-generativeai
- build-python-layer.sh script for rebuilding

**Schema Updates:**
- geminiAnalysis field for full Gemini response
- contentBlocked, contentBlockReason fields
- GCS storage path fields

- dateUtils: shared flexible date parsing
- Atomic draft transitions to prevent concurrent apply race conditions

title: Dimitri/audio clip balance

commits.messageBody:
Three-layer fix for clip audio drifting out of sync (2-4s by end of 8min video):

1. Keep clip audio IN segments (sync by construction):
   - Mode A: clips with audio (speech/ambient) embed source audio at correct
     sample rate (aresample=44100) instead of extracting to separate .aac
   - Mode B: silent clips use anullsrc (unchanged)
   - Probe output for audio stream; remux with silent audio if source had none
   - Removes Phase 3b (build_clip_audio_track) entirely

2. Add silent audio to slideshow segments (crossfade.py):
   - Remux with anullsrc after concat so all segments have consistent
     video+audio streams for the final concat demuxer

3. Rebuild timeline from probed durations (timeline.py):
   - rebuild_timeline_from_actual_durations() walks items using ffprobe'd
     segment durations instead of model predictions
   - scale_timeline_to_duration() scales all positions to match actual
     concat duration (ground truth)
   - Eliminates cumulative rounding errors in music ducking positions

4. Always mix [0:a] with ducked music (audio.py):
   - Removes has_voice_recordings conditional that skipped [0:a] when no
     voice recordings existed — this dropped ALL clip audio when
     audio_classification and has_significant_audio were inconsistent
   - Single path: amix with normalize=0, always reads video audio

Also: three-level ducking (speech/ambient/silent), audio_classification on
VideoClipInfo, per-clip volume control, speech detection service.

Three-phase frontend theming overhaul:

1. Semantic token refactor: migrated ~2,500+ raw Tailwind gray scale classes (bg-gray-*, text-gray-*, border-gray-*) to 27 semantic CSS variable tokens defined via @theme in index.css. Surfaces, borders, text hierarchy, and component tokens (buttons, tracks, placeholders, badges, dividers, skeletons).

2. Light theme: added .light class override in index.css with inverted token values. Tailwind v4 utilities use var(--color-*) at runtime, so all components theme automatically via CSS cascade.

3. Theme toggle: ThemeContext/ThemeProvider, ThemeToggle component with Sun/Moon icons, FOUC prevention inline script in index.html, localStorage persistence. Toggle in app header, landing nav, and project view top bar.

## Summary

Long-running multi-feature branch wrap. The branch accumulated several independent landings over the last few weeks; this PR ships them together so we can stop the bleed and get the work merged.

**Branch is 6 commits behind origin/main** (GCS east4 migration) — will need rebase before merge.

### Major landings

- **Timeline-v2 DnD redesign** — merged-timeline view at `/timeline-v2` with live-rearrange within-section reorder, cursor-positional right→left drop via phantom system, cross-section drag with collapsed-section auto-expand and auto-scroll, left→right drag-to-remove, multi-select (cmd/shift-click, Escape clears, cross-pane auto-clear), and multi-drag (stacked overlay + count badge, source-tile dim, multi-drop across all 4 surfaces). New floating action bar. Spec at `docs/dnd-redesign-spec.md`, steps 1-8.

- **Cost tracking gap fix (A.1 + E.1)** — per-photo upload Gemini analysis and multimodal embedding are now instrumented end-to-end. `analyze_with_gemini` returns `usageMetadata` on every dict path (including safety-blocked); `photoProcessingWorker` fires `trackCost` after photo-update success. `embedImage` accepts optional `projectId`; Cloud Run video processor sends `embeddingCallCount` in callback. Closes open questions #1 and #2 in `docs/ai-inventory.md`. New `PRICING.multimodalEmbedding` ($0.0002/call) in `costTracker.js`. Validated against a real project: \$0.667 fully-loaded for 88 photos + 27 videos + Create Timeline + 1080p render. A.1 is 29% of project cost — single largest line item.

- **Thematic stage model alignment** — `thematicStage.js` reverted from `gemini-3-flash-preview` to `gemini-2.5-flash` to match A.1's safety boundary. Preview model calibration drifted under us and started randomly tripping PROHIBITED_CONTENT on photos A.1 had already cleared, sinking entire thematic batch calls to the timestamp-fallback path. Aligning on 2.5 makes the safety boundary consistent.

- **AI inventory recon** — new `docs/ai-inventory.md` catalogs every AI/ML call site (model, concurrency, cost tracking, downstream consumers, safety-filter handling). Living reference document.

- **Timeline Editing UX Rework Sessions 1-3** — persisted cluster identity (`aiMetadata.clusterGroupId` + `clusterOrigin`), cluster-aware right panel + detail lightbox, drag-and-drop insert + Create Timeline rerun warning. Documented inline in `docs/progress.md`.

- **Other (smaller landings on this branch)** — section sizing bounded-proportional algorithm (1.3× max spread), curator-prompt simplification (objective/description/title/subtitle removed from curator input), draft-clip-ID-leaking-into-exclusion-reasons fix, GCS env-var threading, unified lightbox refactor.

## Test plan

- [x] Backend lint clean (`cd backend && npx eslint src/ --quiet`)
- [x] Backend tests passing (1026 / 52 skipped / 0 failing)
- [x] Backend import check (`node --check src/server.js`)
- [x] Frontend lint clean
- [x] Frontend tests passing (1183 / 567 skipped / 0 failing)
- [x] Frontend build succeeds (`npm run build`)

- [ ] Reviewer: spot-test `/projects/<id>/timeline-v2` for multi-select + multi-drag (4 surfaces: within-section reorder, cross-section, right→left add, left→right remove)
- [ ] Reviewer: smoke-test a Create Timeline run end-to-end on a real dev project (\`/timeline-v2\` is dev-only — main flows should be unaffected, but worth confirming nothing regressed)
- [ ] Rebase onto current `origin/main` before merge (branch is 6 commits behind)

## Known limitations (carried into future polish)

- Click-on-empty-area to clear selection — deferred (Escape + Clear button + cross-pane auto-clear suffice)
- `TimelineV2OtherBucket` doesn't support multi-select (would need synthetic sectionId model)
- Right-pane shift-range falls back to cmd-toggle (shared `ClusterTile`'s `onTogglePhotoSelect` is single-arg, can't read modifier keys)

commits.messageBody:
Contributor (share-code) videos could get stuck at videoProcessingStatus=pending
forever, holding the "Processing" count at 1 and disabling Create Timeline.

Root cause: both video confirm handlers sent the HTTP response and only then
awaited callVideoProcessor. A comment even claimed this was safe, but under
serverless-http the Lambda invocation ends when the response is flushed, so the
post-response enqueue is not reliably executed. It won the race most of the time
(most device uploads worked) and lost it for a contributor video in prod, leaving
no Cloud Task, no error, and a stuck pending. Fix: enqueue BEFORE sending the
response in both handlers; the response now reflects the real dispatch outcome.

Safety net so a stuck pending can never permanently block the user: a scheduled
sweepStuckVideos Lambda (rate(10 minutes)) finds pendings older than 10 min via a
new sparse VideoPendingIndex GSI (PK videoPendingGsiPk='PENDING', SK
videoProcessingStartedAt), re-dispatches up to 3 times (resetting the clock), then
marks them failed (which unblocks Create Timeline). The marker, startedAt, and
videoDispatchAttempts are managed centrally in db/photos.js updatePhoto (SET on
pending, REMOVE on ready/failed) so every status writer stays consistent. Failure
states use error codes mapped to friendly copy in frontend videoErrors.

Migration script addVideoPendingIndex.js (npm run add-video-pending-index) creates
the GSI and backfills existing pendings; IAM grant for the index added to
serverless.yml. Deploying needs the GSI migration (dev then prod) plus a backend
deploy for the scheduled Lambda.

Tests: marker SET/REMOVE in updatePhoto, sweep decisions (re-dispatch vs fail),
and a dispatch-before-response ordering assertion. Docs: DATA_MODEL,
VIDEO_RENDERING, INFRASTRUCTURE, progress, INDEX.

Part 1 - the capture loop:
- New FEEDBACK entity (db/feedback.js) writing adminPk='FEEDBACK' into the existing AdminIndex (third discriminator; keys-then-batchGet read like getAllMusic, projection-independent). POST /api/feedback (any logged-in user), GET/PUT /api/admin/feedback (own admin handler).
- Notification email to FEEDBACK_EMAIL (feedback@kindredreels.com, new provider.environment var). Awaited in try/catch, never fails the submission: an unawaited SES promise can freeze with the Lambda environment and silently drop.
- Frontend: useFeedbackStore (zustand) + one FeedbackDialog mounted in App.tsx; FeedbackButton in the global header (auth-gated, desktop pill + mobile drawer) and both project-workspace bars. Context captured at the trigger: base (route, page, user, version, UA, viewport) + project bundle (media makeup by type/location, memories=has recording vs groups=multi item, music tracks, theme, videos, latestRenderStatus) + lazy sections fetch merged on resolve.
- /admin/feedback triage page: newest-first list, status select, expandable rows with sectioned context detail and notes editing.
- CI: deploy-frontend.yml injects VITE_APP_VERSION=dev-<sha> (prod already used the release tag).
- PARKING_LOT #13: per-endpoint rate limiting recorded as deferred.

Part 2 - the proactive prompts (all call the Part 1 opener, no new plumbing):
- feedbackProjectContext hoisted into a guarded useMemo above ProjectLayout's early returns (old placement could throw in the project-error-with-videos state); shared openProjectFeedback helper for all workspace prompts.
- Render fails while watching: failed-transition effect keeps its toast and opens the dialog (category broken, video id + error). Transition-only, so no re-fire on polls or reloads.
- Already-failed at arrival: onReportVideo on the outlet context, threaded VideosTab -> VideosList; "Report this" chip in the failed row (VideoStatus stays presentational).
- Upload failures: one "Report this" pill in PhotoUpload's completion failure state (owner path only, hidden behind shareCode) with failedCount
  + per-file errors.
- Post-video card: PostVideoFeedbackCard on player close, once per video via localStorage keyed on the stable video id; no category preset.
- Video-ready email links /project/:id/videos?feedback=1; ProjectLayout consumes the param after load and auto-opens the dialog.
- Login returns to the attempted destination: ProtectedRoute preserves path+query in state.from; Login honors it and stashes it in sessionStorage before the Google OAuth redirect; Callback restores it. Paths sanitized to same-app; take is idempotent per page load (StrictMode double-mount otherwise consumed the stash and stomped the redirect with /projects).

Docs: API.md, DATA_MODEL.md, INFRASTRUCTURE.md, FRONTEND.md, PARKING_LOT.md, progress.md updated with Last verified bumps.

## What this is

The watch-page conversion workstream (recon 2026-07-17 → Specs 1 + 3), tracked under bucket 2 in `docs/beta-launch/BETA_LAUNCH_TRACKER.md`.

## Spec 1: watch page & share loop (frontend)

- "Make Your Own" CTAs with distinct `?ref=watch-*` params: end-of-video overlay, below-player block (above the fold on desktop), header outline button, upgraded footer line
- Netflix-style credits mode: 2s into the end credits the video shrinks to a corner tile (credits stay watchable, opt-out link) and the CTA card fills the space; exact timing via new `creditsDuration` in the public video payload; full-scrim overlay remains the fallback
- Player frame capped at ~65vh on laptops so the CTA row clears the fold; mobile full-width buttons
- Web Share text now `Watch "[title]", made together on Kindred Reels` (clipboard stays bare URL)
- index.html meta/OG/Twitter copy updated to current positioning (closes CODE-11)

## Spec 3 Part A: per-video link previews

Bucket 1 step 4. Two testers had reported a dead "edit music" button and a dead
save button; a read-only check found neither still exists. The music UI was
rebuilt after that build and every control is wired, verified live including a
save-reload-persist round trip. Both fix items closed as no-ops.

What shipped instead:

- Per-section music chip in the timeline header: inline play/pause, the track
  name, and an explicit "Change". Sections with no music get a dashed
  "Add music" pill. The swap path used to be a bare tooltip on muted text,
  which testers never found.
- One shared audio player (frontend/src/hooks/useAudioPreview.ts): a single
  module-level Audio element published via useSyncExternalStore, replacing the
  two copy-pasted `new Audio()` blocks in MusicModal and SectionMusicPicker.
  Starting any preview stops whatever was sounding, so "playing one section
  stops another" falls out for free and opening a modal silences the chip.
- Picker reframed so one track is the norm and chaining is the exception.
  Queue chrome (grip + position number) appears only at 2+ tracks; showing
  reorder affordances on a lone track taught testers that dragging was how you
  swap. Choosing a track REPLACES when the section is already covered and
  appends only when silence remains, with an add/replace glyph on the library
  row and a "Replaced X. Undo" line. The old append-then-delete workflow
  produced a placement with no effect.

Renderer bug found while checking whether that stray placement was harmless.

track in a section its natural duration uncapped, so appending to an
already-covered section made the FIRST track run past its own section and mix

mixer, so the audible symptom was never the track you added. Chain members are
now clamped to section.music_end_ms. Two regression tests; verified the clamp
test fails without the fix.

never ticked. Steps 1 and 3 are complete; step 2 is 6 of 10 with four genuinely

Banks 2024/2012. Gate green: backend import check, lint, 1219 tests; frontend

commits.messageBody:
June's DynamoDB bill was $44.10 against $3.66 in May, $43.27 of it in one
line: 346M read units from 2.89M Scans against LoomedMemories-dev over ten
days. Only 922 API Lambda invocations happened in that window, so it was a
local `npm run dev` with a browser tab polling a scan-backed endpoint.

Two scans sat behind routine reads. Both are gone.

getVideo(videoId) was a full-table scan called from 11 sites including two
polled status endpoints. Now a GSI1 query on VIDEO#<videoId>, written by
createVideo. No new index: GSI1 existed with projection ALL and videos were
not using it. Forward-only; pre-existing video records have no GSI1 keys.
The poll that triggered it is also bounded now: YouTubeUploadPanel skips
ticks while document.hidden and gives up after 15 minutes into a `stalled`
state rather than `failed`, since the upload is usually still running.

getAllProjects(userId) scanned the whole table behind GET /api/projects, the
list every signed-in user loads. Replaced with a sparse UserProjectsIndex
(PK userProjectsPk = USER#<userId>, SK created_at). The PK is a dedicated
attribute rather than the bare userId on purpose: userId also lives on
VIDEO#, FEEDBACK#, PROBE_CLICK and other items, so keying on it would make
the index non-sparse. A test asserts userProjectsPk !== userId.

serverless.yml must ship with these: the Lambda role scopes DynamoDB index
access to explicit per-index ARNs with no /index/* wildcard, so without the
UserProjectsIndex ARN the deployed Lambda gets AccessDenied on every
project-list request. This cannot surface locally, which runs on personal
creds.

Index status: ACTIVE on both tables, dev 48/48 owned projects covered, prod
52/52. Prod was backfilled BEFORE this code ships, so the migration must be
re-run immediately after the prod deploy to pick up projects created in the
gap; otherwise they vanish from their owners' dashboards when reads cut over.
Rollout order and command are in INFRASTRUCTURE.md.

Second half: the migration scripts could silently target the wrong stage.
shared/dynamodb.js captured the table once at import and defaulted to dev,
and since ESM evaluates imports before the importing module's body, nothing
could redirect it at runtime. Combined with .env.prod not carrying
DYNAMODB_TABLE_NAME while .env already set it to dev, the repo's documented
prod recipe resolved to the DEV table for every script. Correct for
serverless deploy, which reads the table from serverless.yml; wrong
everywhere else.

Table resolution is now per call, and scripts/lib/requireStage.js makes
--stage mandatory and authoritative: it sets DYNAMODB_TABLE_NAME and
S3_BUCKET from the flag before the first query, announces any override, and
exits 1 when the flag is missing. Nine scripts are guarded. Four of them
carried their own copy of the dev-defaulting fallback; so did
db/importJobs.js and lambdas/cognitoTriggers.js, which build their own
clients, and both now resolve lazily too. Runtime `STAGE || 'dev'` fallbacks
are left alone: serverless.yml sets STAGE on every deployed function, so
they only apply locally where dev is correct.

Backend 1237 tests pass. CloudWatch read-runaway alarms for both stages were
created by hand and are documented in INFRASTRUCTURE.md; they are not IaC.

Note: docs/PARKING_LOT.md in this commit also carries entry 18 from the
settings workstream, which shares this working tree.

Tester feedback from Sachin: hunted for the settings page, then made changes
and could not find the save button. Both reproduced by measurement, not taken
on report. On the two dev test projects the inline Save sat 959px and 1081px
down a 679px viewport, so it was never on screen without deliberate scrolling.

SAVE. SettingsSaveBar is always rendered, stuck to the bottom of the settings
scroller, Save disabled until something changes, Discard shown only while
dirty. That matches SectionSettingsModal and EditTranscriptModal, which
already gated a persistent Save on a dirty check. Sticky rather than fixed:
fixed would span under the desktop sidebar and behind the mobile bottom nav.
The bar owns error display, since every way to produce an error here leaves
the form dirty and so guarantees the bar is on screen.

The dirty baseline lives in SettingsTab.types.ts and is built by the same
projectSettingsFields() that seeds the useState initializers, so the two
cannot drift and open the form falsely dirty. Durations stay strings because
the inputs are text and empty is a valid intermediate state. 10 unit tests.
beforeunload covers leaving the app; in-app tab switches are deliberately
unguarded, since useBlocker needs a data router and the app mounts
<BrowserRouter>.

FINDABILITY. The sidebar entry was already labelled with a gear but sits
below a flex-1 spacer, rendering ~430px beneath the last nav item with
nothing grouping it; collapsed it was an unlabelled 16px gear alone in the
corner. Added a border-t. Kept at the bottom on purpose: it is a utility, not
a step, and the other four carry counts. Added a Settings gear to the
timeline header, where people actually discover they want settings. A real
<Link>, so cmd-click works; TimelineV2PageHeader now takes projectId.

STRUCTURE. All four group headers render through one SettingsGroupHeader,
including Danger Zone via tone="danger"; three had copy-pasted the markup and
the fourth had drifted to a different type scale. Field labels unified.
Dropped a redundant border-t plus pt-8 above Sections that stacked to ~64px
of separation where no other boundary had more than 32. Skipped the spec's
optional in-page anchor nav: it was conditioned on the page being long, and
it is ~1.6 screens after the removals below.

PEOPLE AND HONOREE NAME REMOVED. Adding a person from Settings had never
worked: the frontend sent referencePhotoIds: [] and
createProjectPersonHandler rejects an empty array with a 400. The backend log
showed three attempts, zero persons created. The error rendered ~1000px down
the page, which is why it went unnoticed. Edit and delete were already
duplicated in the People tab, so only the broken Add was unique here. Honoree
Name went with it: tributes own it. handleSave omits honoreeName, and since
the handler only writes honoree_name when the key is present, the stored
value is preserved (verified against a project with a real honoree; no dev
project had the field set at all). TributePeopleSection gained an empty state
and now always renders, so a project with no people does not hit a blank tab.
PARKING_LOT 18 tracks the remaining gap: Create Timeline is still the only
working way to add a person.

FOCUS RING. Every left-column field rendered its focus ring with the left
side sheared off. overflow-auto clips both axes and the fields sat flush at
the left content edge, so the 2px ring, painted outside the border box, had
nowhere to go. px-1 -mx-1 buys it room and cancels the shift. The layout's
own padding is on the parent, outside the clip box, and could not help.

Also: invitation and reminder SMS said "share a memory for null". Both
templates interpolated honoree_name unconditionally, and checked against real
dev data every project was affected, including a tribute (Disney 2018 gave
"for null", Outer Banks 2024 and Pasha gave "for ."). sendInvitationEmail had
branched on this since it was written; SMS never got the same treatment, so a
tribute-era template survived the widening to vacations and events. Both now
share one resolveSubject helper: honoree, else project title, else a
subjectless ask. Subjects cap at 30 chars and truncate with three periods
rather than U+2026, which is absent from GSM-7 and would force the message
into UCS-2, cutting the segment from 160 chars to 70. 11 tests, including a
guard that no message renders "null" or "undefined".

Frontend 1151 tests, backend 1237, lint clean both sides, build clean.

body:
## What was broken

No completed video would play. Prod, dev, and local. Since local was affected too, this was code, not infrastructure.

`getVideo(videoId)` was moved from a full-table scan to a GSI1 query on `GSI1PK = 'VIDEO#<videoId>'`, and the migration was classified **forward-only**: `createVideo` writes the keys, so new videos are fine and old ones were expected to be merely absent from the index.

They were not absent. They were **unreachable**. `getVideo` is the read path for videos that already exist, so once reads moved to the index every pre-existing video returned `null` and its handler returned 404. Three handlers use it, so an affected video could not be played, downloaded, polled for status, or deleted.

Measured before the fix:

| | dev | prod |
|---|---|---|
| VIDEO# records | 144 | 75 |
| completed | 139 | 70 |
| **carrying the keys** | **0** | **0** |

Every video ever made, in every stage.

## The fix

A data backfill, not a behaviour change. `scripts/backfillVideoGsi1.js` sets both keys on any VIDEO# record missing them: `--stage` guarded, idempotent, rate limited, with a coverage check that exits non-zero rather than reporting a false success.

**Already run in both stages** (dev 144/144, prod 75/75), and `getVideo()` verified to resolve a previously-404ing record in each. So this PR records a fix that is already live. A `failed` video in prod was backfilled too, since the delete handler shares the lookup and it could not otherwise be cleared.

No code change was needed for correctness. `createVideo` writes the keys and every later write to a VIDEO# record is a partial `UpdateExpression`, in the Node paths and the Python renderer alike, so nothing strips them across create → processing → complete → share.

## Hardening

The GSI key names were literals in three places: the writer, the reader, and the backfill script. They are now exported from `db/videos.js` and shared. A writer/reader disagreement is silent, producing an empty result and a 404, which is exactly this bug.

The existing `videos.test.js` passes **unmodified**, which is the evidence the refactor preserves behaviour. (A first attempt routed the query through `ExpressionAttributeNames` and failed that test; the indirection bought nothing since `GSI1PK` is not a reserved word, so the constant is used in a template literal and the emitted expression is byte-identical.)

## The rule worth keeping

Recorded as PARKING_LOT 20: **forward-only is safe when only a NEW feature reads the index, and unsafe the moment an EXISTING read path is switched onto it.**

No unit test could have caught this. The suite mocks DynamoDB, so a query returns whatever the test sets up. The tests asserting that `createVideo` writes both keys and that `getVideo` queries the index all passed while every video in production was broken.

## Also corrected

Two stale docs found while writing this up:
- `DATA_MODEL.md` still described the GSI1 migration as forward-only, the exact claim that caused the outage.
- `PARKING_LOT` 19 still read "awaiting index creation" though `UserProjectsIndex` is ACTIVE and backfilled in both stages.

## Checks

Backend 1237 tests pass, lint clean, frontend build clean.

## Deploy note

Nothing to run after merge. The backfill is done in both stages and the code change is behaviour-preserving.

## Why

The prod DynamoDB read alarm fired Aug 3: **964K RCU in one hour** from a dashboard polling the project video list every 3s. Each tick read every video record in the project (7.5MB on the worst project, `ConsistentRead: true` doubling the cost) to return status fields and six integers.

## What

**Stored counts.** `computeVideoCounts` writes `itemCount`/`memoryCount`/`standalonePhotoCount`/`photoCount`/`clipCount`/`recordingCount` on the record at creation; handlers read them instead of recomputing from `videoItems`. Safe because `videoItems` is write-once (only `createVideo` writes it).

**`VIDEO_CONTENT#` split — the actual RCU fix.** `ProjectionExpression` does *not* reduce consumed capacity (DynamoDB charges by item size read; measured 261 RCU with and without), so `videoItems` moved to a sibling item whose SK fails the `VIDEO#` prefix test. **Measured: 261 → 8 RCU per list read.** Also shrinks the GSI1 (projection ALL) copy of every record.

**SQS pointer messages.** Render jobs now send `{videoId, projectId}`; `resolve_video_job` (Python) fetches the record + sibling, and accepts legacy inline messages and pre/post-split records, so old and new deploys coexist. Closes a latent silent failure: inline payloads over SQS's 256KB cap threw on send, the catch swallowed it by design, and nothing re-dispatched — the biggest videos queued forever.

**Frontend read-after-write fixes** (exposed by dropping `ConsistentRead`): generate seeds the videos cache from the response, delete filters the cache, `useGenerateVideo` hook fixed the same way.

## Verified

- Backend 1,253 tests / frontend 1,151 / lints zero-warning / build clean
- Dev migrations run + verified: counts 144/144, split 103 records, 0 unreachable (41 legacy zero-item records correctly excluded)
- End-to-end local render of a 73-item video through the new path, watched successfully
- Real-query verification against dev DynamoDB (projection expression, reserved-word aliasing, RCU measurements)

## After merge

Dev auto-deploys (backend + frontend + renderer workflows). For prod: tag the release, then run
`backfillVideoCounts.js --stage=prod` and `splitVideoContent.js --stage=prod` (bare, not piped through `tee`). Renderer/backend deploy order doesn't matter right now (no prod users; renderer accepts both shapes), noted in VIDEO_RENDERING.md for the future.

The prod DynamoDB read alarm fired Aug 3: 964K RCU in one hour from a
dashboard polling the project video list every 3s. Each tick read every
video record in the project (7.5MB on the worst project) with a
consistent read, to return status fields and six integers.

- Store the six item counts on the VIDEO# record (computeVideoCounts,

- Move videoItems to a VIDEO_CONTENT#<videoId> sibling item: the prefix

  size read), which is why the split exists; migrated via
  splitVideoContent.js (dev done, prod pending)
- SQS render jobs are now pointer messages {videoId, projectId};
  resolve_video_job fetches record + sibling and accepts legacy inline
  messages and pre/post-split records. Closes a silent failure: inline
  payloads over SQS's 256KB cap never dispatched and nothing surfaced it
- getProjectVideos: allowlist projection (status/error aliased; reserved
  words) and no ConsistentRead; ProjectLayout seeds the videos cache
  from the generate response and filters it on delete instead of
  refetching (eventually consistent readback could strand the tab)
- getItem helper: type-based arg disambiguation + options passthrough
- Docs: DATA_MODEL, VIDEO_RENDERING (deploy order: renderer before

… Timeline trust

Four changes plus the tracker rewrite, closing the friends-and-family feedback bucket. A read-only recon first established what had actually shipped versus what the tracker claimed: step 5 (settings) shipped Aug 2 in 4d5b1d3 with every box left unticked, the same failure mode as steps 1-3 in d3ed124. New standing rule in the tracker decision log: a commit completing a tracker item updates the tracker in the same commit. This commit does that.

WORDING. The two live "Excluded" strings in PhotoLibrary (filter chip label, dropdown option) become "Not Included", matching the timeline everywhere else. The internal `excluded` key is untouched: it is the filter value, matched against filterMode and the <option value>, not copy. The lightbox "Why Excluded" heading stays by decision; it names a per-item reason, where "Not Included" names a location. Two further occurrences are dead and left alone: ExclusionReasonBadge reaches users only via OrganizationPhotoGrid, which has no importer, and OrganizeStage only via AIProducerPage, which is not routed in App.tsx.

TYPE SCALE. Targeted, not the app-wide pass the tracker carried since July. Column-intro descriptor/count lines and the per-section count band 14->16px, the sections chip 10->12px. TimelineV2SectionHeader's collapsed-row counts went 12->14px, NOT 16: that row packs title, music chip, counts and kebab onto one line where everything but the title is 12px, so at 16px the counts would match the title's size, outweigh the music chip beside them, and eat the title's truncate budget. The spec said this line was text-sm; it was text-xs, so "text-sm -> text-base" was not executable as written. Measured in Chrome rather than assumed: 16/16/12/14, html and body still 16px (no global leak), all four section rows scrollWidth === clientWidth with zero title truncation. index.css and every @theme block are untouched.

CREATE TIMELINE TRUST. "Nothing is final yet. You can edit the timeline afterward and recreate it anytime." now renders in all three length branches, above Create. It previously existed only in the 40+ branch as a text-xs footnote under the length label, so everyone below 40 weighted items committed with no reassurance at all. It lives in CreateActionButtons, the one component all three branches render, so they cannot drift and "exactly once" is structural rather than a convention; the old footnote is deleted. The Additional settings collapsible gained "These choices are starting points too. Recreating the timeline lets you change them." Those options really are rerun-only, and the copy says so instead of implying in-place editing.

ConfirmRerunTimelineModal reframed from destructive warning to normal action: "Recreate your timeline?", a body stating what is kept (photos, people, description) against what is reset (hand edits), primary styling, and RotateCcw in a primary tint replacing the danger-tinted AlertTriangle. The rerun is still destructive to hand edits and still gated; only the framing changed, because the rest of the flow now tells users the timeline is a starting point and this modal was contradicting it. Its 4 tests follow the new copy.

RECREATE IN THE TIMELINE HEADER. Icon-only, leftmost in the cluster and deliberately as far as possible from Create Video: the two are otherwise one click apart and only one is reversible. It navigates to photos?createTimeline=1, the deep link TimelineEmptyState already uses, so there is exactly one Create Timeline flow, no lifted state, no second modal, and the existing rerun confirmation still gates it. Gated by the same MIN_MEDIA_FOR_TIMELINE check and the same rejected-clip-stub filter as the Library button, because the deep link is guarded on the other side and an ungated button would navigate and silently do nothing. Desktop only: below 768px TimelineV2Tab renders MobileTimelineView, which imports none of these components.

Closed without action after the recon: video-ID-in-title (stale, no code path renders an id in any title or the video-ready email), People-section-optional (no matching surface exists), single-image drop flicker (the tile changes React key twice on drop, phantom -> optimistic temp id -> server id, the second unmitigated; accepted until a real user reports it). Curation-quality candidates removed from the tracker by decision. Length-only rerun without re-analysis -> PARKING_LOT 21.

Also carries the video-list migration status from the working tree, unrelated to bucket 1: backfillVideoCounts and splitVideoContent are now done in both stages (OPERATIONS.md script table, progress.md entry).

Verified in the browser on a real project, not only in tests: filter and lightbox wording, computed font sizes and overflow, all three length branches, the rerun modal, and the header Recreate round-trip. Frontend 1151 tests, backend 1253, lint clean both sides, build clean.

body:
Four commits. The first three are bucket 8 phase 5 and its verification; the fourth is an unrelated fix to render progress that came out of testing a 4K render on dev.

## Bucket 8 phase 5: the pricing probe (`c302bec`)

Gate prompts now name what a plan costs after the beta, a plans modal shows all four, and pressing unlock records a probe click. Until now `recordProbeClick` had sat in the client with zero callers since phase 3, so the beta collected no willingness-to-pay signal at all. Verified PROBE_CLICK# was empty on both stages first, which is the only condition under which the source vocabulary can be extended for free.

- Prices live once per side as integer cents, asserted at start to be integers ascending along the ladder, with the exact values pinned in both test suites so a one-sided mirror edit fails a test.
- `PROBE_SOURCES = [...GATE_SOURCES, 'settings']`, derived rather than hand-copied. The two lists differ on purpose, and `'settings'` must stay out of `GATE_SOURCES` because `services/entitlements.js` throws on an unrecognised gate source. A test asserts that divergence directly.
- `logProbeClick` returns `void`, so no call site can await it and no later edit can put a network round trip in front of a tier grant.
- Surfaces: a plans modal mounted once, a tier badge at all three places a project title renders, and a read-only Plan section on settings that contributes nothing to the dirty baseline.

Two corrections found while building: `probe_version` is the integer `1`, not the string the spec named (the endpoint validates `Number.isInteger`), and `AdminFunnel.tsx` held a third hardcoded copy of the prices, so a price change would have left the page they are measured on quoting the old number.

Verified end to end on dev across three journeys, each recording the source it should: `settings` from the badge, `resolution` carried through a gate-to-overview handoff, and `collaborators` from a direct gate unlock.

## Brake drill and change 9 (`b816279`, `a6aa56a`)

Invite-only proven on the deployed `preSignUp` by invoking it with synthetic Cognito events, so no accounts were created. Four cases held, including the two the code comments claimed but nothing had tested: the Google branch is gated too, and an emailless signup is refused rather than waved through. Reverted and re-verified afterwards.

Change 9 (transcription invocation stopped) verified on the deployed path: a new recording carries `transcript_status: none` with `transcript_started_at` null, and `transcriptionWorker` shows zero invocations. A July recording on the same project still reads `failed`, which is the state the change existed to stop producing.

Also records a standing deploy rule: while tier gating lives on an unmerged branch, a backend deploy carries the enforcement and must be paired with a frontend deploy from the same branch. A backend-only deploy re-opened exactly the window the phase 4 build order was inverted to avoid.

## Render progress rebuilt (`99fcfae`)

Unrelated to the tier work. The 4K render meant to test the previous ETA fix showed the fix would have been inert: its blend keyed on `completed / num_workers`, the box has 16 CPUs, and every sample was past item 30 of 116.

Measuring properly found a larger problem. Percent came from ~15 hardcoded literals plus a `phase_weights` table, and nothing tied a band's width to how long it takes. Across 955 seconds, downloads were 23% of wall time inside 10 bar points and the tail 4% inside 25. Seconds-per-percent ranged 1.6 to 22.4 in one job.

`video/progress_model.py` prices every unit of work in wall-clock seconds. Pooled work divides by the worker count and serial work does not, so the three execution regimes fall out of the model rather than fighting it. Percent and ETA come from the same budget and are consistent by construction. A runtime calibration absorbs error in the constants, so only their relative weights matter. Resolutions generalise through one exponent anchored on recon A's 4.94x, which this render vindicated.

New RENDER_TIMING# records store predicted against measured per work kind, so the cost table can be refitted from real renders. Until now the renderer timed everything and lost it, because the EC2 box has no CloudWatch log group and stops itself after each job.

Net 372 lines removed against 219 added, including `render_eta_seconds`, `RENDER_TIME_MODEL`, `estimate_render_seconds` and the constant override that pinned the ETA at 75s for seven minutes.

## Verification

157 python, 1437 backend, 1296 frontend tests. Both lints at zero warnings, `tsc -b` clean, frontend build succeeds.

**Not yet exercised:** no real render has run against the new progress model. It is tested against the recorded trace from the 955s render and against a simulation of the orchestrator's exact call sequence, but replaying a trace is not the same as driving ffmpeg. The first render after this deploys is the real test.

## What merging deploys

Backend to dev Lambda, frontend to dev S3, and the EC2 renderer via `deploy-processing.yml`, which also carries the dead-code deletion from Aug 8 that has never shipped. Prod is untouched, since it is gated behind a `v*` tag.

Worth watching on the first render: `calibration` on the new RENDER_TIMING# record. 1.0 means the cost table was right; the old model would have scored 1.60 on that render.

commits.messageBody:
Two tracks that share the frontend API surface, so they land together.

PROBE (changes 0-7). The tier allowlist in funnelHandler held the
pre-four-tier ['free','basic','plus','premium'], where 'premium' meant the
OLD top tier rather than the new $24 middle one. Renamed to the locked four
after confirming zero PROBE_CLICK# records exist on either stage, so nothing
strands. Fixed a latent bug found by the new test: sendResponse takes two
parameters, so `sendResponse(res, success(click), 201)` silently dropped the
201 and the endpoint had always returned 200. Thirteen sibling handlers use
the correct `success(data, 201)` form; this was the only outlier, and it
survived because the endpoint has never had a caller and had no test file.

Probe clicks were the only funnel metric not stranger-segmented, despite
userId already being present and matching the exclusion-list key. Added
byTierStrangers and distinctStrangersByTier additively, leaving byTier and
distinctStrangers with their exact prior meaning so snapshots stay comparable.
This had to land before any probe UI ships: snapshots are immutable, so a
snapshot written unsegmented loses that day's segmentation permanently.

Enriched the record with price_amount, probe_version, source and from_tier
before the UI exists, since retrofitting later would split the dataset.
Supplied-but-malformed values return 400 rather than being dropped, because a
dropped value would make the record indistinguishable from one predating
enrichment. price_amount is never defaulted to 0 on read: missing is not $0.

Admin funnel gained a four-tier table sorted by ladder order rather than
count, since where clicks fall along the price ladder is the signal.

TRANSCRIPT (changes 8-9). Removed the voice-memory transcript UI and stopped
the invocation, so new recordings never acquire pending or failed state.
Recon corrected two premises: no failed or pending transcript record has ever
existed on either stage (prod holds 37 working transcripts from January, all
in one founder-owned project), and the EC2 renderer contains a complete
caption burn-in path, live but inert because the field is always null. The
renderer is untouched. System B, the self-hosted Whisper clip speech
detection in Cloud Run, is operational and deliberately fenced off.

Removing TranscriptSection orphaned selectedRecording and refetchRecordings,
which existed only to serve it; the whole chain is gone rather than left
implying a live refetch path.

Verified: 1306 backend tests, 1151 frontend, lint clean both sides, tsc -b
clean, and browser checks confirming the memory panel still plays audio and
System B still renders clip speech transcripts.

commits.messageBody:
The beta brake. Both limits live in one file, config/limits.js, so lowering
one in an incident is a one-line edit in an obvious place rather than a search
through handlers.

No count existed to enforce against. getPhotoCountAndFirst queries every
PHOTO# item in a project, and ProjectionExpression does not reduce RCU, so
checking a cap that way would have re-created the pattern the August DynamoDB
work removed. Measured on dev while investigating: the projects list already
reads 6,960 items and 2,535 RCU per single load. That is logged as
PARKING_LOT #25 under bucket 5 rather than fixed here, because the same query
also selects the list thumbnail and cannot simply be deleted.

Instead, atomic ADD counters on the PROJECT# record, following the
recordShareView precedent, since bulk imports make lost updates the normal
case rather than the edge. The upload counter increments inside createPhoto so
no write path can forget it: there are four writers, and Google Photos import
was missed by the original scope precisely because the count lived outside the
write. Uncapped, it would have made the limit decorative. Import truncates and
reports rather than rejecting a batch the user already picked.

Extracted clips never count. They are derived by the pipeline, not uploaded,
and run to 20% of PHOTO# items on real projects.

Both counters are lifetime, not current inventory, and deleting does not give
the allowance back. The cost this caps is incurred at upload and rebuild time
and is not refunded, so a current-inventory counter would let upload-delete-
repeat run up unbounded analysis spend. The user-facing copy says so rather
than suggesting removal helps.

Counters live in db/projectCounters.js rather than db/projects.js on purpose.
Putting them in projects.js created a photos.js to projects.js import, and 22
test files mock that module; under ESM a mock missing one export fails the
whole suite at load. That coupling was the cause of an intermittent suite
failure seen during development.

Verified live against dev: counter increments for a photo and a video, skips a
clip, reads back correctly through the transform, and blocks at the limit.

commits.messageBody:
Projects carry a tier, the app gates five capabilities on it, and accepting a
gate prompt upgrades the project in place. Free during beta, so the grant is
direct; phase 6 wraps the same function in Stripe.

BUILD ORDER, INVERTED ON PURPOSE. The spec put backend enforcement before the
frontend prompt. That would have left a window where every dev project reads
Free and 1080p renders, invites and voice all 400 with no UI to recover.
Frontend gating landed first instead, so the loop was demoable and nothing was
ever blocked. The tradeoff, stated plainly, was that gating was bypassable by
direct API call until enforcement landed. Nothing deployed in between.

THE LADDER. config/tiers.js is the vocabulary: TIER_ORDER, TIER_ENTITLEMENTS,
the resolution and length orders, the gate sources. Each tier is a strict
superset of the one below, which is what lets every check be "is my tier at or
above the lowest tier offering this" rather than a lookup table of exceptions.
The file throws at load if the organizer gains a length mode nobody priced.

VALID_PRICE_TIERS moved here out of funnelHandler.js so the probe allowlist and
the entitlement ladder cannot drift apart. The probe source vocabulary was
corrected while it was still free to do so, verified zero PROBE_CLICK records on
either stage: tribute-creation became tribute, and the missing voice was added.

services/entitlements.js holds the checks and is deliberately DB-free. Nine
handlers import it, and a db/projects.js import here would have recreated the
ESM mock breakage that produced db/projectCounters.js. The write lives in
services/tierGrant.js for that reason alone. grantTier is upgrade-only, same
tier is a success no-op with no write, and it contains no authorization,
because phase 6's webhook authorizes by signature rather than by route.

NO SILENT CLAMPS. An explicit above-tier request gets a 400 naming the tier
needed. Quietly rendering 720p when the caller asked for 4K is a lie the caller
cannot detect. Omitted-field defaults became tier-aware instead:
organizeEventHandler defaulted videoLength to a hardcoded standard, which is
itself above Free, so every Free project that omitted the field would have
failed a gate on a value it never asked for. defaultLengthFor clamps down only.
Premium and Tribute still default to standard, per the bucket 1 finding that
long auto-generated videos are rarely what people want.

RESOLUTION HAD NO VALIDATION AT ALL. req.body.settings was spread verbatim into
the persisted render job, and get_resolution in processing/src/video/models.py
resolves an unknown name with .get(name, DEFAULT). A typo rendered silently at
720p and read as a renderer bug. Junk is now rejected, above-tier is gated, and
absent is left alone because the 720p default is inside every tier.

VOICE IS FOUR HANDLERS, NOT TWO. The recon undercounted. Two run without
ownership middleware and load the project themselves: the public
completeMemoryHandler, and recordDraftMemoryHandler, which is mounted with
verifyToken only and carries an explicit no-ownership-check note. The public
recording upload delegates to the authenticated handler, so it attaches the
project it loaded before delegating; without that the delegate would have read
an absent project as Free and refused a contributor recording on a project
entitled to it. An absent project reads as Free everywhere, so the gates fail
closed if a future route forgets its middleware.

MINTING VERSUS HISTORY. Gates enforce actions, not history. No project was
backfilled; absent reads as Free through the transform. Existing recordings,
share codes and rendered videos on a Free project keep working, and no code is
revoked. Enabling timeline sharing gates its reactivate branch as well as its
create branch, because putting a switched-off link back into the world is the
same act as minting one. Resending an existing invitation is not gated.

CONTRIBUTORS ARE HIDDEN FROM, NOT PROMPTED. Someone holding a share code cannot
upgrade anything, so an upgrade prompt aimed at them is a dead end. Two public
share responses carry a derived capabilities.voice boolean and never the tier
name, which would only leak what the host pays for. Absent means permissive on
the client, so neither a cached response nor a stale deploy can hide a recorder
that works.

TWO REGISTERS FOR TIER NAMES. Rendered sentences use display labels; everything
machine-facing stays raw lowercase. That covers the stored attribute,
VALID_PRICE_TIERS validation, TIER_ORDER comparisons, the probe fields, and the
requiredTier field on a gate's 400. A copy audit caught the backend saying "the
standard tier" beside a prompt saying "Standard", which is one user seeing two
names for one product.

TWO SHAPES OF CONTROL HAD TO CHANGE on the frontend. The resolution select
became a button group: a disabled option cannot be clicked, so the native
control physically could not open the prompt or, in phase 5, log the probe
click. Locked length rows are likewise not disabled. Gate the trigger, not the
panel. Browser verification earned its keep by catching a gate placed on the
VoiceRecorder panel instead of on the Record Memory button that is its only
route in, so it never fired; the unit tests mounted the panel directly and
could not have caught it.

ALSO IN HERE. The invite-only brake, option B: a flag and email allowlist in the
existing PreSignUp trigger, enforced per branch so an existing user can still
link Google, plus the three frontend error-handling gaps the recon found. And
the render ETA fix, whose stale constant turned out to live in two files, not
one; renderer.py is the one driving the user-visible progress report.

Found along the way and left alone: MemoryModal, DraftMemoryModal and
ShareProjectModal have zero live mounts, and ProjectLayout's
InviteContributorModal has no opener. Gated anyway where it was cheap, but four
dead modals is worth someone's attention.

Backend 1428 tests green, lint clean at --max-warnings 0. Frontend 1226 green,
lint clean, build succeeds. Processing render-estimate tests green.

enforcement, including a 720p and a 1080p render to check the ETA fix; the
length gate live, which costs a real analysis run plus a rebuild against the
cap; and the brake drill, which needs a dev deploy because preSignUp is a
deployed Lambda. Unit tests cover all three, which is not the same thing.

Found by running a real 82-item 4K render to verify yesterday's ETA fix. The
fix had not taken effect, and two further defects were sitting underneath it.
None of the three were visible from the code: the existing tests checked the
estimate arithmetic in isolation and passed throughout, because every one of
these lives in the seam between computing a number and getting it on screen.

THE FIX HAD GONE INTO A FUNCTION WITH NO CALLERS. orchestrator.py calls
create_video_from_items and nothing else. Yesterday's 45.0 -> 14.5 edit landed
in create_video_with_metadata, which nothing calls. The live function still
held 45.0, and the render proved it: ceil(82/8) = 11 batches x 45.0 + 15 =
510s, exactly the 8m30s on screen. The constant is now module-level and DERIVED
(SEGMENT_ETA_SECONDS_HD x SEGMENT_ETA_4K_RATIO) rather than typed in, so the
relationship is visible and a test can assert the ratio against recon A instead
of against a magic number. The HD anchor stays at 8.0: it is this path's own
calibration and no per-SEGMENT timings have ever been recorded.

A FLOAT COST EVERY RENDER ITS FIRST ETA, SILENTLY. boto3 rejects Python floats,
estimate_render_seconds returns one, and update_video_progress catches its own
exceptions and only logs. So the dispatch-time estimate never reached the
record and the UI sat on "calculating" until the per-segment callbacks took
over a minute or two later, with one ERROR line the only evidence. Fixed at
both ends: the call site casts, matching what the per-segment callback twelve
lines below already did, and update_video_progress coerces defensively. A
function that swallows exceptions must not also trust callers to honour a type
hint nothing enforces. The log line now formats from the same coerced values it
writes, so it cannot disagree with the record.

THE RUNNING ETA IGNORED THE WORKER POOL. (elapsed / completed) x remaining
assumes items finish serially. With 8 workers nothing completes until roughly
one segment-duration has passed and then a whole wave lands, so the first
measurement is about 8x too slow and the estimate then collapses as 1/n:
104m, 52m, 35m, 26m, 21m, 17m, 15m, 13m, across eight items that finished
within seven seconds of each other. Replaced by a shared render_eta_seconds
that weights the measurement by completed / num_workers and leans on the static
estimate until a full wave lands. It replaced FIVE copies of the naive formula,
not four: report_progress's fallback is reachable after all, via the title and
credits slide reports that pass no estimate of their own.

DEAD CODE DELETED. create_video_with_metadata and create_parallel_video, 535
lines between them, zero callers anywhere, each carrying its own copy of the
per-segment constant and the ETA math. That duplication is not theoretical: it
is what stranded yesterday's correction in code that never runs. A warning
comment would have been weaker than deletion. create_video_from_items is now
the module's only entry point, and both functions are gone from video/__init__
and __all__. Two imports they alone used (DEFAULT_DURATION, PhotoInfo) went
with them; both are still exported from video/__init__ via .models, which is
where orchestrator.py gets PhotoInfo.

Tests: new test_render_progress.py, 15 cases across the three defects,
deliberately covering the seams rather than the arithmetic. It pins the ETA
blend against the real numbers from the log above, asserts the 4K ratio against
recon A's measured slopes, checks a float eta and a float percent are both
written as ints while an absent eta stays absent, and guards the mistake itself
by asserting the live entry point is the one the constants feed.

Note for anyone adding tests here: pytest.approx is unusable in this venv,
numpy is architecture-broken and only shimmed for what conftest needs.

Verified: 146 processing tests pass, up from 131. Ruff findings across
processing/ are 45 before and 45 after, the same set; the new test file is
clean. Backend 1428 tests and lint unchanged, frontend builds.

NOT verified live: the corrected 4K constant predicts ~4m30s where the old one
said 8m30s for this render, but that comparison needs a deployed dev render.
RENDER_TIME_MODEL was fitted on prod EC2 (m6i.4xlarge, 16 workers) and a local
run on 8 workers measures the laptop, not the model.

shows all four, and pressing unlock records a probe click. Until now

(0/900/2400/7900) and its mirror in utils/entitlements.ts. The backend
asserts at start that they are integers ascending along the ladder, on the
same guard pattern as the existing LENGTH_ORDER check, because a mispriced
middle tier would render a nonsense plans list with nothing else going wrong
to point at. Both test suites pin the exact cents, so a one-sided edit to a
hand-kept mirror fails a test rather than shipping a prompt reading $24
against a record reading 900.

The probe's source allowlist stops being a hand copy. config/tiers.js now

asserts that divergence directly, since it otherwise reads as a bug worth
"fixing".

Fire and forget is structural rather than a convention. logProbeClick in
utils/probe.ts returns void, so no call site can await it and no future edit
can put a network round trip in front of a tier grant. It reads the price
from the constants itself, so what gets stored is by construction the number
the UI displayed. The click is reported BEFORE the grant, so a grant that

overview handoff, and 'collaborators' from a direct gate unlock. The funnel

commits.messageBody:
The 4K render that was meant to test the previous ETA fix showed the fix would
have been inert. Its confidence blend keyed on `completed / num_workers`, the
box has 16 CPUs, and every observed sample was past item 30 of 116, so the blend
sat at 1.0 throughout and the code reduced to the naive rate it replaced.

Measuring that render properly found a larger problem than the ETA. Percent came
from about 15 hardcoded literals in orchestrator.py plus a `phase_weights`
table, and nothing tied a band's width to how long the band takes. Across 955
seconds: downloads were 23% of the wall clock inside 10 bar points, rendering
72% inside 65, the tail 4% inside 25. Seconds-per-percent ranged from 1.6 to
22.4 within one job.

Three further causes the old model could not express. Rendering runs in three
regimes, not one: a 16-worker Pool, a serial loop over slideshow runs, and
serial title and credits slides; a single items-per-second rate cannot describe
all three, and the observed collapse from 609s to 75s fell exactly on the
pool-to-serial boundary. Units cost wildly different amounts while the counter
treated a 4K clip and a slideshow photo as the same "1 item". And a constant
override, `estimated_remaining = estimated_render_time * 0.2`, outranked every
computed value and pinned the ETA at exactly 75 seconds for seven minutes.

video/progress_model.py prices each unit of work in wall-clock seconds: clips by
duration, slideshow runs by photo count, downloads by item count and
deliberately not by resolution, since fetching a photo costs the same whatever
it is later encoded into. Pooled work divides by the worker count and serial
work does not, so the regimes fall out of the model rather than fighting it.

Percent is done_work/total_work and ETA is k*remaining_work from that same
budget, which makes them consistent by construction: elapsed/(elapsed+eta)
reduces to the percent. The budget is built before the first download and runs
through upload, so the bar spans the whole job instead of restarting.

The constants are estimates and the design assumes it. A runtime calibration
k = elapsed/done_work converges on their error within the first few units, so
only the relative weights have to be right, which is the requirement the old
model failed hardest. Early estimates lean pessimistic deliberately: a render
that beats its estimate reads as pleasant, one that overruns reads as stuck.

Resolutions generalise through one exponent, (pixel ratio)^0.73, anchored on
recon A's 4.94x for 4K that this render vindicated (955s actual against 596s
from the OLS fit then in use, 822s from the multiplier). Fitting each resolution
separately needed data that does not exist: 480p had zero measured renders, and
1080p's five produced a row implying 1080p costs less per item than 720p.

New RENDER_TIMING# records store predicted against measured per work kind so the
cost table can be refitted from real renders. Until now the renderer timed every
segment and phase and lost all of it, because the EC2 box has no CloudWatch log
group and stops itself after each job. Write failures are swallowed: a lost
measurement must never fail a finished video.

Deleted as superseded rather than annotated, following the August lesson about
stranding corrections in dead code: render_eta_seconds, the SEGMENT_ETA_*
constants, RENDER_TIME_MODEL, estimate_render_seconds, the phase_weights table
and the constant override. Net 372 lines removed against 219 added.

Tests replay the real 955s trace and walk the orchestrator's exact call sequence
end to end, since the budget is driven from two files across a job that only
runs on an EC2 box.

body:
Follow-up to #190. Two commits, both driven by measurements from three instrumented renders of one 112-item project on dev: **720p 184s, 1080p 286s, 4K 932s**.

## What the renders proved

The structure held. The ETA crossed the pool-to-serial boundary — where the old model collapsed 609s to 75s — and went 151 → 131 → 118 instead. No collapse, no freeze, and the predicted total stayed within a 15s band the whole way.

The constants were 4-5x off, in specific and now-measured ways.

## `5794d9f` — fitting the model

**The resolution exponent was anchored on the wrong quantity.** Every row derived from one exponent fixed on recon A's 4.94x for 4K. But 4.94 is a *whole-render* ratio, diluted by work that doesn't scale, and this model separates that out, so its scalars have to be encode-only. Measured encode-only ratio at 4K is **6.99**, with two independent segment kinds agreeing to 0.01. The whole-render ratio measured here was 5.83, right next to recon A's number, which is what confirms the two were measuring different things. Measured rows are used directly now; only 480p, still never rendered, falls back to a curve.

**A correction to #190's claim.** That PR said downloads were 23% of wall time inside ten bar points, citing 224s. That figure was extrapolated from the old render's item rate, not measured. Downloads are 10-11 seconds, 1-6% of a job. The real distortion is rendering taking 85-97% of the clock for 60 of 100 points while the tail takes 2-9% for 25. Seconds-per-percent varied **19x** inside a 4K job, worse than the 14x claimed, and grew with resolution.

**Three structural bugs no tuning would have fixed.** Upload was budgeted at 310s, 41% of a 720p job, and never completed inside the renderer because it happens after the render returns — the bar stalled below 60% then jumped to 100. Slideshow runs were planned as one aggregate unit but completed one per run. Section titles, memories and single photos were rendered but never planned.

## `fb5d16f` — reconcile and damping

`5794d9f` claimed to plan every kind the renderer completes and only added section titles. `SEG_MEMORY` and `SEG_PHOTO` were still unplanned, about 5% of a job's work with no budget behind it.

Guessing the split would be wrong, since the orchestrator genuinely can't know it before items exist. So `JobBudget` gains `replan()`, and the renderer reconciles every segment kind once composition is known, immediately before the pool starts. Clips and memories are sized by real mean duration, slideshow runs by actual mean photo count.

Also added `SCALE_DAMPING`: measured 720p to 4K, encode segments run 6.99x but slides run 4.16x and 4.67x, concat 3.45x, and verify 1.0x. Applying the full scalar to all of them over-priced 4K by ~60%.

## Result

| | predicted | actual | k |
|---|---|---|---|
| 720p | 171.6s | 156.5s | 0.91 |
| 1080p | 282.3s | 266.9s | 0.95 |
| 4K | 942.6s | 913.3s | 0.97 |

Within 9% at every resolution and slightly high in each, which is the intended pessimism. The same renders scored 0.21, 0.26 and 0.45 before.

## Verification

173 python, 1437 backend, 1296 frontend tests. Both lints at zero warnings, `tsc -b` clean, build succeeds. A plan-versus-complete symmetry check confirms no kind is completed without being planned, planned without being completed, or defined but unused. A new test class pins the table against all three renders so a future edit by intuition fails a test.

**Not yet exercised:** no render has run against this fitted version. The previous build produced the data it's fitted to.

**Known limitation:** constants are fitted to one project's mix of 38 clips and 56 photos, so clip-versus-photo weighting is still confounded. A lopsided project would separate them.

title: Fit the render progress model to three real renders

commits.messageBody:
Three renders of one 112-item project (720p 184s, 1080p 286s, 4K 932s) replaced
the shipped estimates with measurements, and corrected two things I had asserted
without measuring.

THE EXPONENT WAS ANCHORED ON THE WRONG QUANTITY

Every resolution derived from one exponent fixed on recon A's 4.94x for 4K. But
4.94 is a WHOLE-RENDER ratio, diluted by downloads and other work that does not
scale, and this model separates those out, so its scalars have to be encode-only.
Measured encode-only ratio at 4K is 6.99, with two independent segment kinds
agreeing to within 0.01 (6.99 and 7.00). The whole-render ratio measured here was
5.83, sitting right next to recon A's number, which is what confirms the two were
measuring different things. Anchoring encode cost on a whole-render figure
under-read 4K encode by 30%. Measured rows are used directly now; only 480p,
which has still never been rendered, falls back to a curve.

THE PERCENT DISTORTION WAS REAL, THE MECHANISM WAS NOT

The previous commit said downloads were 23% of wall time inside ten bar points,
citing 224 seconds. That was extrapolated from the old render's item rate, not
measured. Instrumentation put downloads at 10-11 seconds, 1-6% of a job. The real
distortion is that rendering is 85-97% of the wall clock and got 60 of 100
points, while the tail is 2-9% and got 25. Seconds-per-percent still varied 19x
inside a 4K job, worse than the 14x claimed, and it grew with resolution because
fixed bands cannot follow where the time actually goes.

THREE STRUCTURAL BUGS NO AMOUNT OF TUNING WOULD HAVE FIXED

Upload was budgeted at 310 seconds, 41% of a 720p job, and never completed inside
the renderer because it happens after the render returns; the bar stalled below
60% and then jumped to 100. Slideshow runs were planned as one aggregate unit but
completed one per run, charging the fixed cost once and crediting it sixteen
times. Section titles, memories and single photos were rendered but never planned
at all, so they completed work the budget had never accounted for.

RESULT

The fitted table predicts all three renders within 9%, slightly high in every
case, which is the intended pessimism: 171.6s against 156.5 at 720p, 282.3
against 266.9 at 1080p, 942.6 against 913.3 at 4K. The same renders scored 0.21,
0.26 and 0.45 before this pass. Music stopped scaling with resolution, having

floor dropped to 0.15, since 720p measured 0.206 and the old 0.25 clamp bound.

commits.messageBody:
Closes the gap left by the previous commit, which claimed to plan every kind the
renderer completes and only added section titles.

RECONCILE

SEG_MEMORY and SEG_PHOTO were completed by the renderer and never planned by the
orchestrator, so roughly 5% of a job's work landed with no budget behind it
(7.9s at 720p, 12.6s at 1080p, 41.3s at 4K). It was partly self-cancelling,
because the orchestrator planned all 74 downloaded photos as slideshow work when
only 56 became slideshow runs, but two errors roughly cancelling is not a fix.

Guessing the split would be the wrong repair: the orchestrator genuinely cannot
know it, having only photo and clip counts before video items exist. So JobBudget
gains replan(), which REPLACES a kind's planned cost, and the renderer calls it
for every segment kind once the composition is known, immediately before the
pool starts and only a few percent into the job. Clips and memories are sized by
their real mean duration rather than an assumed one, and slideshow runs by their
actual mean photo count. Percent is already clamped monotonic, so moving the
denominator can stall the bar but never walk it backwards.

WEAKLY-SCALING KINDS

Applying the full encode scalar to everything over-priced 4K by about 60% for
several kinds. Measured 720p to 4K: encode segments 6.99x, title slide 4.16x,
credits slide 4.67x, concat 3.45x, verify 1.0x. Slides render less pixel-bound
work than a segment, concat is a stream copy touching containers rather than
pixels, and verify probes the container and measured 0.1s at every resolution.

Added SCALE_DAMPING, an exponent applied to the segment scalar per kind (0.70,
0.81 and 0.62 respectively), and moved VERIFY into the unscaled set alongside
downloads, upload and music.

Also aligned the music-track planning assumption, which was 3 for the mix and 2
for the download of the same tracks.

A plan-versus-complete symmetry check now passes: no kind is completed without
being planned, none is planned without being completed, and none is defined but
unused.

body:
Follow-up to #191. One commit, driven by two renders against the fitted model.

## The constants were right, the path was not

Calibration landed at **0.868 at 720p and 0.866 at 4K** — near-identical across a 9x pixel range, with every significant kind between 0.7 and 1.1. The model predicts well.

But a watched 4K render showed 22 minutes, then 16, then 19, and peaked at a **41-minute prediction for a job that took 15**. An estimate that wanders reads as unreliable even when it lands close, which is the whole point of showing one.

## Why

A single global factor, `elapsed / work_done`.

Elapsed keeps climbing while a 16-worker pool fills, and at 4K the first clip does not land for about two minutes. Across that dead zone the ratio exploded, and it was then applied to every remaining kind. Being global also meant downloads overrunning their budget inflated the estimate for encode work that was perfectly calibrated, and every crossing between phases of differing speed moved the whole number.

## The fix

Each kind now carries its own measured-against-predicted ratio, applied to its own remaining work. A kind with no completions yet contributes its **prediction** rather than anything derived from another kind's timings, so the dead zone produces no change at all. The global fallback sums MEASURED time instead of elapsed, so time in which nothing finishes cannot inflate it.

Replaying the same render's shape:

| | old | new |
|---|---|---|
| dead zone (34-185s) | 1010 → 2318 | 1116 → 1146 |
| peak prediction | **2452s** (2.7x truth) | **1146s** (1.2x) |
| settled | 1013 → 937 | 933 → 917 |

The displayed finish time is smoothed rather than the countdown, asymmetrically: shrinking lands at once because it is good news, growing is approached slowly because that is what reads as broken. Smoothing the finish time rather than the remaining seconds is deliberate, since a steady finish time makes the countdown tick down by itself.

## Messages

These were written for debugging, not for an audience: `Rendering 116 items at 4K with 16 workers`, `Rendered memory 1/1`, `Rendered section title 48/116`, `Concatenating segments`, `Mixing 4 music tracks with ducking`, and worst of all `Rendered slideshow (6 photos)`, which dropped the counter entirely and so read at 88% as though fresh work had appeared.

The render phase now speaks with one voice and one running count: **`Building your video (23 of 116)`**. A person waiting on a video does not need to know that a slideshow run differs from a video clip, and watching the wording lurch between internal stage names is what made steady progress look erratic.

All copy lives in one block with the house rules stated. A test asserts no internal vocabulary, no em dashes, and that the count cannot overshoot the total.

## Also

The status line rendered `Time remaining: ~1m 49s remaining` — the label and the formatter both supplied the word. A test now asserts it appears once rather than trusting three text anchors. Section titles refitted from 24.1s measured against 62.9s predicted at 4K.

## Verification

183 python, 1437 backend, 1297 frontend tests. Both lints at zero warnings, `tsc -b` clean, build succeeds.

**Not yet exercised:** no render has run against this version. It is tested against a replay of the 4K render's shape, which is not the same as driving ffmpeg.
