commits.messageBody:
The progress work fixed most of what was wrong and the remainder is one bounded
defect, so it goes to the triage inbox rather than consuming more time.

Fixed and not to be re-litigated: percent is time-proportional (seconds-per-
percent spread 19x down to ~1.4x), the cost model is calibrated from three
instrumented renders (0.868 and 0.866 at the two ends, every significant kind
0.7-1.1), resolution scaling is measured rather than extrapolated (6.99x encode
from 720p to 4K, two kinds agreeing to 0.01), the late-render estimate holds
within a few percent, the 609s-to-75s collapse and the seven frozen minutes are
gone, and the messages read as English.

Still wrong: on a 4K render the predicted total climbs for roughly three minutes
(914s at 40s elapsed, 2006s at 205s, against a true total near 930s) before
descending and settling correctly. 720p does not show it.

Root cause is recorded so it does not need rediscovering. `_measured[kind]`
charges every second since the previous completion to whichever kind completes
next, so summing it returns approximately total elapsed and makes
`_global_ratio` algebraically almost identical to the `elapsed / done_work` it
was written to replace. `_kind_ratio` then falls back to that figure for kinds
with no completions yet, contradicting its own docstring. At 4K the expensive
clips have no completions for about two minutes and get priced at a ratio
inflated by pool spin-up. The fix is two changes: do not charge a kind for the
lead-in before its first completion, and price an unobserved kind from its
prediction rather than the global.

Also recorded is the process lesson, which is the part most likely to save time:
the simulation that validated the design passed because it modelled a clean
empty dead zone, while the real render interleaves cheap completions through it,
each absorbing the accumulated dead time into its ratio. Build the replay from a
captured trace, not a hand-written shape. The five traces are named in the
archive entry.

commits.messageBody:
Everything needed to charge for a plan now exists, is tested, and is off.
PAYMENTS_ENABLED ships false and a test pins it there, so no charge path is
reachable and beta behavior is byte-identical to before.

The whole thing hangs off one route. POST /api/projects/:projectId/tier was
already the only way a plan could change, so it became the seam rather than a
second route beside it. Flag off it grants. Flag on, a strict upgrade gets a
Checkout session and the response is a URL instead of a plan, and nothing is
granted until the webhook confirms payment. Everything that is not a strict
upgrade behaves identically either way, so the flag cannot change the error
surface.

The frontend learns which mode the server is in from the shape of that response
and nothing else. No flag endpoint, no build-time switch, no second source of
truth. useGrantProjectTier owns the branch; both priced surfaces go through it.

The riskiest line is a mount order. Stripe signs raw bytes and this app parses
JSON globally, so the webhook mounts above express.json() with express.raw().
Below it, every webhook would fail verification and the only symptom would be
upgrades paid for and never granted. The test signs real payloads with a real
HMAC and includes a case that feeds the handler a parsed body, so moving the
mount fails a test instead of failing silently.

Idempotency needed no mechanism: grantTier has treated a re-grant as a no-op
with no write since phase 4, so a Stripe redelivery costs nothing. Status codes
to Stripe are retry instructions, split on whether a retry could help.

Prices did not move into Stripe. Sessions use inline price_data read from
TIER_PRICES, so config/tiers.js stays the one place a price can change and
amounts are the difference between two entries.

Verified end to end with test cards on local and on deployed dev, in both flag
states, including redelivery, decline, abandon and the return-to-tab path.

Also lands the probe bySource follow-up: source dimensions on the funnel
snapshot, the tier-by-source matrix on /admin/funnel, and the kept count script.

The recon that preceded this found the premise was wrong. This work was scoped
against a belief that AWS costs about $150 a month. It costs eight. The one bad
month was June at $57.29, and $44.10 of that was the DynamoDB read-runaway the
late-July work already fixed, now $0.93. There was no runaway cost problem left,
only a gap in noticing.

AWS now has one budget at $50 with rungs at $25 and $50. Steady state sits six
times under it and the worst month on record sits just over. Deleting the old
budget mattered as much as adding it: Learning AWS had a one cent limit, covered
the whole account, ran to 2087, and had been permanently in alarm since 2021, so
every budget email this account ever sent was noise.

GCP took two tries. The first budget was set at $75 from an estimate off our own
cost events, and the console says real spend is about $66 a month, so its first
rung would have fired every month. That is the same failure as the deleted AWS
budget, introduced one day later. It is now $200. It pairs with the pre-existing
OpenClaw Budget rather than replacing it: this one sees gross consumption while
credits last, that one fires when credits stop covering.

The estimate was wrong for a reason worth keeping. Cost events capture about a
third of GCP spend. Networking is the second largest line at roughly $21 a month
and we track none of it, which is the cross-cloud egress the consolidation
decision warned about. Vertex AI, the one genuinely per-project line, is
undercounted by 39%. Recon A's per-project figure is optimistic on its largest
component; margins hold but the number is not precise.

Credits are not a launch concern: $2,555 remains and the 2028 grant alone
outlasts its own expiry at current burn.

Two investigations closed as no defect. The Rekognition gap was a manual backfill
script run once in June plus face-vector storage, with production's empty table
explained by the 90-day TTL rather than broken instrumentation. The ETA
verification item was superseded by the August work-budget rebuild, which was
fitted to the very renders it asked for.

Bucket 8 moves to DONE. All six phases complete, exit criteria met.

body:
Four days of work on the contributor upload path, prompted by a real prod failure.

**Note on scope:** this branch also carries the theme and credits work that was already uncommitted in the tree. Four files (`videoHandler.js`, its test, `progress.md`, `VIDEO_RENDERING.md`) contain both efforts interleaved, so they could not be split cleanly. Confirmed before committing that the theme work is ready to ship.

## What prompted it

A contributor batch of 168 items froze twice in prod. I traced it through CloudWatch, DynamoDB and S3: the trigger was the uploader's own network, and a third attempt after a restart pushed all 168 items in 42 seconds on unchanged code. But the two failed runs exposed defects that turned a recoverable blip into permanent damage.

## Upload resilience

Both upload paths PUT the file with a bare XHR that had an `error` listener and nothing else. A socket that stalls without erroring never settles its promise, and since uploads run through a fixed pool of five workers, each hung promise took a worker slot out of circulation for good.

New `utils/api/uploadTransfer.ts`: a stall watchdog that aborts after 60s without movement, retry with backoff, and an `AbortSignal` so Cancel actually cancels. Deliberately **not** `xhr.timeout`, which caps total duration and would kill a legitimate 1GB upload on a slow line. What separates a dead socket from a slow one is movement.

## Orphan cleanup

`pending_upload` video records are written before their bytes exist, and nothing ever revisited them, so a dead browser left Library cards stuck on "Uploading..." forever. `sweepStuckVideos` gains a third pass on a new `UPLOAD#PENDING` partition of the existing sparse GSI. Past 90 minutes (the signed URL only lives 60, so the PUT can no longer succeed) it checks GCS: bytes present means the PUT worked and only the confirm was lost, so it finishes the confirm's job; bytes absent means the record goes.

## Dedupe

Device uploads had no duplicate check at all, on either path. Identity is a server-computed SHA-256 of name, size and lastModified. The read is one snapshot per batch, which also replaced the per-item Google Photos check that ran a full project query for **every** media item (168 full-project queries on a 168-item import).

## Group share links

`createShareCode` always accepted an omitted name; only the modal forbade it. The substantive work was underneath: `CONTRIBUTOR#` records and `PHOTO#.contributor_id` were two unrelated id namespaces, bridged only by a case-insensitive **name** match that collapses two contributors sharing a first name. Rows now carry `deviceId` and are created on first actual upload, following the existing credits principle of contributed content over invitations. Credits group by `contributor_id` so a mid-session rename is not credited twice in a finished video.

## Also

- Contributor badges name the uploader or say "You", matching on device id for the same reason.
- Fixed a latent 401: `PhotoUpload` branched on `shareCode && contributorName`, so an unnamed contributor fell through to the **authenticated** endpoint. Unreachable only by an incidental guard, which group links made load-bearing.
- `PhotoUpload.test.tsx` was `describe.skip` with 56 assertions against a component that no longer exists. Replaced with 20 covering current behaviour, including regression locks on the 401 and on Cancel.
- `matchMedia` stubbed in the shared test setup (a jsdom gap, not a fact about one test).

## Checks

Backend 1566 tests, frontend 1388, lint and build clean on both, re-run after the merge from main.

## Not verified

None of this has been exercised end to end against a real dev environment. The group share link flow in particular (mint, arrive, name, upload, owner's Contributors tab) has only been unit tested. Worth a manual run on dev before it goes near prod.

Docs: `API.md`, `DATA_MODEL.md`, `PIPELINES.md`, `VIDEO_RENDERING.md`, `progress.md`, PARKING_LOT #26 and #27 closed, plans in `.claude/plans/`.

body:
Three fixes after testing #195 on dev. Two were not where either of us expected.

## The group-link toggle went into dead code

I built the "One person / A group" toggle into `ShareProjectModal`, which **isn't rendered anywhere in the app**. The live surface is `InviteToAddPhotosModal`, opened from the Photo Library. That's why dev behaved exactly as before.

`ShareProjectModal` and its test are deleted.

## Adding photos is never per-person, so the question is removed

Not made optional, not a mode. The old "Who are you inviting?" field bound the code to one `CONTRIBUTOR#` record, and from then on `validateShareCode` handed **that person's name to every visitor**, which is the opposite of what a link posted to a group should do. So the field wasn't merely unnecessary, it actively broke the group case.

Inviting someone to **record a memory** is the genuine per-person case and is untouched.

Copy now says photos and videos, which the flow has always accepted.

## A second person on a shared device inherited the first person's name

I claimed in #195 that this already worked. It didn't, and I'd only tested the empty-browser path.

Checked dev rather than reasoning about it: both recent share codes have `recipientContributorId = None` and the backend correctly returns a null name. The backend was innocent. The name came from `localStorage`, under a global `contributorName` key scoped to neither project nor share code, and the arrival prompt only fired when that value was **empty**.

The prompt now appears on **every** arrival on a group link, prefilled from what's remembered, so the common case is one tap on Save and the second person sees and corrects the name. On a per-person link it never appears, since the host already supplied the name.

**Known limit, accepted rather than hidden:** the device id is also a single global key, so two people genuinely sharing one device still land on one contributor row underneath. Confirming the name is what makes that visible when it happens. Recorded in `progress.md`.

## "Invite contributor" did nothing, and it predates this week

Confirmed against `git show --stat`: none of those files are in my earlier commit.

`InviteToRecordModal` is `z-50`; the timeline lightbox it launches from is a `z-[60]` overlay with an opaque backdrop, and the two are **siblings in the same stacking context**, so the modal opened and rendered behind it. `AddPhotosToMemoryModal`, launched from the same provider, was already `z-[70]`, which is what made the inconsistency findable. Raised to match.

## Checks

Backend 1566 tests, frontend 1345, lint and build clean on both, re-run after the merge from main.

New tests include regression locks named for the cases you hit: "asks again even when the browser already remembers a name", and "never asks who is being invited".

## Not verified

The z-index change and the reworked modal layout have not been seen rendering. Both are reasoned, not observed. Worth a glance next time dev is up.

body:
Three contributor-flow fixes found by testing in prod with real people.

## 1. Google Photos was unavailable to contributors

Every `/api/google-photos/*` route sits behind `verifyToken`, and a share-link visitor has no account. The tab was rendered unconditionally in `AddPhotosModal`, so contributors were offered something that could only ever 401. Confirmed live: both endpoints the tab calls return `401 No authorization header provided`. Owners were unaffected throughout.

Built the feature rather than hiding the tab: **six public share-code routes** covering OAuth, picker session create and poll, import, and import status.

### Where a contributor's Google credentials live: nowhere durable

The callback keeps **only the short-lived access token**, under an opaque handle in a new `GPGRANT#` row, and **discards the refresh token**.

Holding a live Google grant on behalf of somebody who has no account with us, cannot see that we hold it, and cannot withdraw it is a liability worth more than the convenience it buys. The cost is a reconnect per import session and a ceiling of roughly an hour per import.

### Because it is a public surface, most tests are about what it refuses

- The share code is read from the **OAuth state**, not the request body, so consent cannot be bound to a project of the caller's choosing
- A grant handle is scoped to project **and** share code, so one lifted from a link cannot be replayed against another
- The import ignores any `projectId` in the body and uses the validated share code's
- The handle is spent on use
- Import status will not return a job from another project

### How the investigation went wrong first

Prod logs showed `GET /api/google-photos/auth-url` reaching the app, which I read as proof the caller was authenticated. It is not: that `📥` line comes from a **global middleware at `server.js:202` that runs before `verifyToken`**, so a 401 logs identically to a success. That single inference produced a detailed and entirely wrong theory about the OAuth app being in Testing mode. The contradicting evidence was in the same logs the whole time: no "Full auth URL" line, meaning the handler never ran.

## 2. Duplicate detection matched nothing

The key hashed in `lastModified`, which **changes when a file is copied, AirDropped or re-downloaded**, so the same photo arriving from a second device looked new. It also made the key unreconstructible, since the value was consumed and never stored: **1 of 361 photos in a real prod project had a key.**

The key is now `name + size`, with `lastModified` stored raw so a stricter key stays possible without another migration.

Two backfill scripts, **already run against both stages**: 1,976 records keyed on dev, 3,886 on prod, and they surfaced **180 duplicate groups already sitting in prod**.

Note this is the only part of the PR that changes behaviour for existing data.

## 3. Contributor videos spun forever after upload

The page fetched its list exactly twice, on mount and once after an upload, so a just-uploaded video's spinner was frozen until a manual reload. It now polls while anything is processing and stops when nothing is, mirroring `usePhotos` rather than inventing a second idiom. The polling decision is extracted as `hasWorkInProgress` and unit-tested directly, rather than by waiting out real 5-second intervals.

## Checks

Backend 1596 tests, frontend 1356, lint and build clean on both.

## Not verified

**The Google Photos flow has not been run end to end.** No real OAuth round trip has happened against these routes: popup, Google, callback, picker, import. The unit tests cover the logic and the refusals, but not the live path. Given it is a new public surface handling someone else's Google credentials, worth exercising on dev before prod.

Docs: `API.md`, `DATA_MODEL.md` (GPGRANT# and the reasoning), `FRONTEND.md`, `OPERATIONS.md`, `progress.md`, PARKING_LOT #28 opened and #29 closed.

body:
Fixes the "Preparing import..." hang you hit on dev.

## What was wrong

After the picker finishes, it counts the selected items before starting the import. That call had **no public twin**, so it hit the authenticated `/api/google-photos/sessions/:id/media-items` and 401'd, leaving the contributor on the spinner forever.

Your console output named it directly:

```
GET .../api/google-photos/sessions/57ed790e.../media-items  → 401
Polling error: Authentication failed. Please sign in again.
```

I built six public routes in #197. The flow needed seven.

## What I did differently this time

Rather than fix the one call that failed, I audited **every** API call reachable on the contributor path. Two more were authenticated-only:

**`deletePickerSession`** is best-effort cleanup whose error was already swallowed in a `catch {}`. Skipped for contributors rather than given a public route: Google expires picker sessions on its own, and it isn't worth widening the public surface for a call whose failure is already ignored.

**Cancel Import** is now hidden for contributors rather than exposed. This one is a judgement call worth stating plainly: cancelling **deletes the photos the job already imported**. A public version would let anyone holding the share link cancel and delete from the owner's in-flight import. That is not a trade I would make for a marginal button on a short import.

## Tests

Three for the new route, including that it refuses a grant handle presented with a different share code. The describe block is named for how it was missed, so the gap is legible if it ever reopens.

Backend 1599, frontend 1356, lint and build clean.

## Note on the branch

#197 was merged while I was working, which left my checkout on `main`, and I committed this fix there before noticing. Nothing was pushed to `main`: the commit was moved onto this branch and local `main` reset to match origin.

body:
Uploading a 1089.2 MB video from prod produced three identical stuck videos in YouTube Studio and a modal that spun forever. Three separate defects.

The worker PUT the whole file in one request with duplex: 'half', which reads like streaming but applies no backpressure, so S3 delivered faster than YouTube accepted and memory pinned at exactly the 1024 MB ceiling. No EventInvokeConfig meant AWS applied its default of 2 retries, each of which re-initiated the upload and got a fresh session URI, hence three partial videos from one request. And an OOM kill terminates rather than throws, so the catch that writes 'failed' never ran; two prod records sat at 'uploading' forever, one since 2026-05-24.

All three are fixed by one mechanism: ask YouTube where it got to and continue from there.

- 8 MiB ranged S3 GETs into Content-Range PUTs. Peak memory is now O(chunk).
- The session URI is persisted BEFORE the first byte goes out, so a retry resumes rather than starting a second upload. That write ordering is the fix for the duplicates.
- Running low on time, the worker re-invokes itself and resumes. Capped at 12 continuations to stay under AWS recursion detection, whose hop counter is per request-chain and not resettable.
- A 200 on the offset query means the upload finished and only our write was lost; recovering the id there is what stops that becoming a duplicate.
- maximumRetryAttempts: 1, explicit. Not 0, because a resuming retry is a free recovery; not 2, because that was the implicit default being left.

Progress reporting falls out of the chunking: bytes are written after each chunk, throttled to a 2% step or 3 seconds, and the status route derives the percent so the panel and the video list cannot disagree.

sweepStuckVideos gains a fourth sweep on a YT#PENDING partition of the existing sparse GSI. The threshold is 60 minutes but the real guard is an updatedAt staleness check, since a live upload touches the record constantly.

Two adjacent bugs fixed while in here. "Upload Again" left the old youtubeVideoId and youtubeUrl, so a poll landing in the gap returned the previous video's link alongside status 'uploading'. And the 409 guard now allows a takeover after 5 minutes of silence, which resumes rather than restarts, so a transient failure no longer locks the user out until the sweep.

The success panel now says YouTube is still processing and the link will not play for others yet. YouTube shows an API-uploaded video as "Uploading 0%" for minutes afterwards, which reads as a failure even to someone who just watched it succeed in the logs.

Verified end to end locally on a 1 GB video: killed at 35%, resumed from YouTube's own byte offset (2 MiB ahead of our record, which is the "trust the Range header" rule earning its place), uploaded the remaining 677 MB, landed exactly on the total, and produced one video instead of three.

title: Dimitri/music start timing

commits.messageBody:
A short project with no section cards opened with eight seconds of silence
and the music arrived half a second AFTER the first photo.

_open_section_timing gave every section a music_start_ms of
current_ms + SECTION_MUSIC_DELAY_MS. Both builders add the title slide's
duration before any section opens, so for a section WITH a card that 500ms
lands inside the card and music gets the whole card as a runway. For a
card-less video current_ms is already the end of the title, so the same rule
put music after the first photo. Same clock time, opposite effect.

One rule now covers every section: music begins 500ms into the slide that
PRECEDES the section's content. With a card that is the card. For a card-less
FIRST section it is the title slide. Measured on a default project (8s title,
from project.titleSlideDuration), card-less music moves 8.5s -> 0.5s and
carded videos are unchanged. Only the first card-less section borrows the
title, so a later one cannot run backwards over the section before it.

Also deletes beat_sync_mode and music_lead_in_ms from
build_authoritative_timeline. They existed to give a card-less first section
a different start and never once affected the audio:
rebuild_timeline_from_actual_durations has no such parameters, and it is the
REBUILT timeline that music placements are re-anchored to in renderer.py, so
the beat-sync start was computed and thrown away before every mix. The
orchestrator passed music_lead_in_ms=0 outright. A regression test now
asserts both builders agree. The separate beat-sync feature that sets photo
DURATIONS from phrase boundaries is untouched.

Trimming a clip in the timeline lightbox reported success, but reopening it
showed the original boundaries. DynamoDB held the new ones the whole time.

useOrgDerivedData builds organizationPhotoMap, which is what the lightbox
reads clip boundaries from. It seeds the map from the photos query and then
OVERLAYS the video-builder items on top, and the overlay wins. onClipSaved
invalidated only ['project', id, 'photos'], so that query refetched the
correct values and the untouched video-builder cache stamped the old ones
back over them. useVideoBuilder carries staleTime 60s, so it would not
refetch on its own either. The dev log shows the PATCH followed by
GET /api/photos and no GET /api/projects/.../video-builder.

New utils/queryInvalidation.ts exports invalidateProjectItemData(queryClient,
projectId, {photoId?}), covering photos, photo-library, video-builder,
memories, stats, plus the single-photo detail key. Undefined projectId is a
no-op so route params pass straight in, and it returns the settled promise so
optimistic mutations that await in onSettled keep their ordering. Applied at
24 call sites.

Six more instances of the same bug, found by the audit:
- TimelineV2 excluded lightbox: onSuccess and onClipSaved, photos only
- useUpdatePhoto: no video-builder, so editing a timeline photo's date,
  description, location or section left the timeline showing the old value
- useDeletePhoto: no video-builder and no memories, so a deleted photo
  survived in the timeline cache
- PhotoDetail deletion: photos + stats only
- TimelineV2 section delete: items move back to the library but photo-library,
  the query feeding the Photos tab, was never invalidated
- MobileTimelineView never passed onClipSaved, so a clip trimmed on a phone
  invalidated nothing

Two non-bugs cleared. TanStack v5 matches keys by PREFIX unless exact:true, so
invalidateProjectData in ProjectLayout was invalidating ['project', id] and
then four keys already covered by it; the four are gone. SettingsTab had
['video-builder', projectId], segments in the wrong order matching nothing,
harmless only because the call above it covered everything. Removed, with its
now-unused queryClient.

The helper alone would not have prevented this, since the original bug was a
call site hand-writing a shorter list than its neighbours.
queryInvalidation.test.ts walks the source tree and fails on any raw
invalidateQueries against photos, photo-library, video-builder or memories,
naming file and line. Verified by reverting useDeletePhoto on purpose. stats
is deliberately outside the guarded set: nothing merges it, and
useGenerateVideo is right to invalidate it alone. Two optimistic-reorder
rollbacks in TimelineV2 are allowlisted and now say why they stay narrow.

commits.messageBody:
Trimming a clip so its thumbnail frame fell outside the new range replaced a
working thumbnail with a broken image. The frame was there the whole time.
The URL was spelled wrong.

media_utils.py names every extracted frame ZERO-PADDED,
f"frame_{second:02d}s.jpg", so GCS holds frame_02s.jpg through frame_16s.jpg.
photoHandler.js rebuilt it unpadded. Trimming a clip to 2-7.8 picks midpoint
4.9, snaps to 4, and wrote frame_4s.jpg against a bucket holding
frame_04s.jpg. It breaks on any single-digit second, so most short clips; the
other nine clips in the test project survived by rounding to 6, 8 and 8. The
reader side was always fine, since /frame_(\d+)s\.jpg$/ parses 06 as 6.

Two more 404s hid on the same line. Frames run from one interval to
frame_count * interval (media_utils numbers them (i+1)*sample_interval and
stops at the video duration), and the old
Math.round(midpoint / interval) * interval was clamped to neither end: a clip
near the start could name frame_0s.jpg, which is never extracted, and one near
the end could name a frame past the last one taken.

The rule now: re-pick the thumbnail ONLY when we can name a frame that was
actually extracted AND that lands inside the trim. Anything less certain keeps
the existing thumbnail, because a frame slightly outside the trim still shows
the clip while a URL for a frame nobody uploaded shows a broken image. New
backend/src/utils/frameNames.js owns the padding, parsing and the
snap-and-clamp; nearestExtractedFrameSecond needs the source video's
frame_sample_interval AND frame_count, and returns null when either is missing.

Four hand-written copies of the padding rule collapse to two, one per language.
media_utils.py exports frame_stem / frame_file_name, used by its own extractor
and by both call sites in gemini_client.py. The backend mirrors it. Both files
name the other. services/video-processor has no test suite, so
frameNames.test.js carries the shared case table and is the only executable
statement of the contract; parity with the Python was verified by running the
same table through frame_stem.

Self-repair instead of a migration: a thumbnail URL that parses but is not in
canonical form is re-derived on the next trim, so bad records fix themselves
as clips get edited. Without it the one currently-broken clip would have
stayed broken, since its frame IS inside its range and the old check would
have called it fine.

commits.messageBody:
The cover picker only ever offered the photos already in the video. Often the
shot that works as a title slide is one deliberately left out of the timeline.

Not just a picker change. orchestrator.py resolves the title photo from
photo_id_to_local_path and clip_id_to_clip_info, both derived from the VIDEO
ITEMS, so a cover outside the timeline is never downloaded and would fall
silently through to get_last_photo_path. The user would pick a cover, see no
error, and get a different title slide.

Picker: two tabs, "In this video" (the existing grid, still the default,
section accordion intact) and "All photos". Tabs appear only when there are
library photos, so the single-source case looks unchanged. No new query, since
usePhotos already holds every project photo; selectLibraryCoverCandidates
filters an array that is in memory. Wired at both picker sites, the Create
Video modal and the Settings tab.

Dispatch: when titleCoverPhotoId is not among the built videoItems (checked
through memory photos too), videoHandler fetches it and attaches
settings.coverPhoto = {photoId, storagePath, mediaType}. Its own field rather
than a smuggled video item, so it cannot reach the video body or the photo
counts and the renderer never has to ask whether an id is a timeline member.

Renderer: fetch that one object after the main photo download and register it
in photo_id_to_local_path, leaving every branch below unchanged. Deliberately
NOT added to all_photos_to_download, which would run it through face
detection, inflate the progress budget's photo count, and risk it reaching
built_video_items. A failed fetch is never fatal; it logs and auto-selects.

Photos only: a clip cover needs its whole source video downloaded to extract
one frame, so clips stay choosable from the timeline tab where that video is
fetched anyway. A deleted cover still falls back silently rather than failing
a render, and the picker now says the photo is gone.

Two preview paths would have lied. resolveCoverPhoto gains an
explicitOnlyCandidates argument: an explicit cover may be any project photo,
but the FALLBACK must stay "last photo in the last section". Passing library
photos in candidates instead would let one win the fallback, since it carries
no sectionId and would survive to the unsectioned last resort.
MobileTimelineView also scanned only timeline items for its theme preview, so
a cover chosen on desktop previewed the wrong photo on a phone; it now takes
allPhotos, already in useProjectContext, so still no new query.

Already correct and untouched: the sticky-cover rule in eventOrganizerHandler
(its comment already said timeline membership does not matter here), and the
watch page and share OG image, which call getPhotoById directly.

Ships in two halves: the renderer change only reaches production on an EC2
deploy, so release the backend and the renderer together.

aws s3 sync sets NO Cache-Control unless told to, and neither workflow told
it to. Verified live: index.html and the JS bundle both came back from
CloudFront with no Cache-Control at all. A response without one gets heuristic
freshness from the browser (roughly 10% of its age since Last-Modified, no
revalidation), so a deploy can stay invisible to a returning visitor for hours.
CloudFront invalidation cannot help: it clears CloudFront, not the copy in
someone's browser. DEPLOYMENT.md said the opposite and is corrected.

Two passes now, in deploy-frontend.yml and deploy-prod.yml. Pass 1 takes
everything except index.html with public, max-age=31536000, immutable, safe
because Vite content-hashes those filenames. Pass 2 takes index.html alone with
no-cache, because it is the file that names the current hashes.

--delete belongs on pass 1. Exclude/include filters apply to the DESTINATION
listing too, so a pass filtered down to index.html can prune nothing and stale
bundles would accumulate forever. Pass 1 excludes index.html, so its --delete
leaves the entry point alone and removes only assets no longer built.

commits.messageBody:
Clicking play made the page appear to scroll itself, sometimes leaving the
player entirely out of view. Three stacked causes, each hiding the next.

1. THE PANEL COLLAPSED. The stage holding the animation band and the player had
no height of its own; it was whatever its in-flow child happened to be. On play
the band went absolute while the video grew from height: 0, so for a moment
nothing was in flow and the panel fell to its padding, 458px to 70px. That
pulled 388px out of the document and every section below jumped up. Measured,
not inferred: scrollY never changed and no scroll event fired in either the
broken or the fixed case. The page was never scrolling; the document was
shrinking underneath it.

The stage now owns its height and animates between band height and player
height, with both children absolutely positioned so neither can decide how tall
the panel is. Height never passes through zero. The measurement also moved off
the band, the one element whose layout role changes at exactly that moment, onto
the stage, whose width comes from its parent and means the same thing before,
during and after. h-[430px] md:h-[360px] became named constants because the
stage needs them as numbers.

2. SCROLL ANCHORING WAS MOVING THE PAGE FOR US. The invisible one. Chrome
adjusts scrollY to keep visible content still when things resize, which is right
for a late-loading image and wrong for a panel that grows ~200px deliberately.
Measured: scrollY went 668 to 824 with no scroll of ours. overflow-anchor: none
on the scrolling element while playing, restored on cleanup.

3. SCROLLING DURING THE GROWTH DOES NOT WORK. A layout change under an in-flight
scroll cancels it. The scroll now waits for transitionend on the stage's height
(700ms fallback for when the height does not actually change) and measures the
settled panel, so the result is exact rather than predicted from Tailwind
spacing. It centres the panel under the fixed chrome when it fits and top-aligns
under it when it does not, so the top of the video is never behind the nav on a
short window. Verified landing at 124px against an ideal of 123px.

The chrome offset is read from the nearest declared scroll-margin-top rather
than by measuring a bar: #transformation already carries scroll-mt-24 for the
"See How It Works" anchor, so that is the page's own statement of the distance,
and it survives the landing page using <nav> where the app shell uses <header>.

The stage's height is a plain CSS transition rather than a motion value, because
it decides the document height and the rendered value should always be the value
the component just computed. Under reduced motion the transition is omitted.

Two environment lessons, recorded in FRONTEND.md: the CDP automation browser
cannot verify this work. scrollTo({behavior:'smooth'}) is a complete no-op in
it, and the height transition renders only intermittently while the inline style
is always correct. Both were mistaken for code bugs before that was understood.

Beta launch bucket 15. Seven critical-path flows in Playwright, run against a real stage (local dev, deployed dev, or prod) from a manual workflow that gates nothing.

Built from `reports/2026-09-11-testing-recon/REPORT.md`.

## Why these flows

The recon measured backend 42% lines, frontend 22%, processing 24%. The distribution mattered more than the totals: **every route-level page on a critical path sat at 0%** (`Login`, `NewProject`, `ProjectsList`, `ProjectLayout`, `SettingsTab`, `PhotoLibraryTab`, `WatchVideo`, all 3,027 lines of `timeline-v2`), while the layer directly underneath was well covered (`utils/api` 48%, `entitlements` 100%, `useTierGate` 100%). So a browser suite adds the missing tier and duplicates almost none of the unit tests.

## What is here

- `frontend/e2e/smoke.spec.ts`: sign in, create a project, upload a photo and a 2s clip, save a settings change, see the tier gate and dismiss it, create an invite link and open it in a fresh browser context, delete. Serial, one shared project, deleted in `afterAll` even when a flow fails partway.
- `frontend/e2e/homePage.spec.ts` rewritten as a signed-out check, which is what distinguishes a broken stage from a broken login.
- `frontend/e2e/sweep.ts` (`npm run test:e2e:sweep`) for a run that was killed outright.
- `.github/workflows/e2e-smoke.yml`, `workflow_dispatch` only with a dev/prod stage input.
- Two e2e Cognito users created, both subs plus the old `user@example.com` sub added to `funnelExclusions.js`.

The old suite was dead, not merely stale: `globalSetup` clicked a `Continue` button the one-step login form no longer has, threw, and Playwright then ran nothing at all. `projectPage.spec.ts` was stale in three further ways; `example.spec.ts` tested playwright.dev. The three-browser matrix went too, having stranded nine projects on the old test account.

## Two rules it lives under

1. **It never accepts a tier-gate prompt.** Accepting routes through `useGrantProjectTier`, which logs a probe click first. That record is the beta's willingness-to-pay signal, is not removed when the project is deleted, and lands in immutable snapshots. Any tier the suite needs comes from `POST /api/projects/:id/tier`, which writes none.
2. **It costs about 1 to 1.5 cents per run** in photo and clip analysis, measured from the live cost-events table. Hence manual dispatch only, and **no deploy workflow may reference it**.

## Also fixed

The deployed DEV frontend bundle carried the **production** GA measurement ID. Every build runs in Vite production mode and so reads `.env.production`, and `deploy-frontend.yml` overrode `VITE_CDN_BASE_URL` for dev but not the GA ID. Verified by curling the live bundle; fixed with a `VITE_GA_MEASUREMENT_ID: ''` override.

## Merge triggers two dev deploys

`backend/**` and `frontend/**` both changed, so merging fires `deploy-backend.yml` and `deploy-frontend.yml` (dev). The backend half is already deployed to dev manually; the frontend half carries the GA fix.

## Status

- Green twice in a row locally against `npm run dev`, sweep confirms zero leftovers.
- **Not yet run from Actions.** GitHub will not dispatch a `workflow_dispatch` workflow until the file is on the default branch, even with `--ref`. So the Actions run against dev has to happen after this merges.
- Lint, unit tests and build pass on both backend and frontend.

body:
Two commits. `03a18b4` is the delete cascade refactor, the CI gate and the skipped-test cleanup. `2842893` is the follow-on work below.

## The one that matters: 234 public frames from deleted prod projects

Cloud Run writes video thumbnails to `thumbnails/<projectId>/<videoId>/` in the CDN bucket under its own identity. The delete cascade never swept that prefix, because the backend service account had no binding on either CDN bucket and every delete would have 403'd. Both CDN buckets grant `allUsers` `roles/storage.objectViewer`, so a thumbnail outliving its project stayed readable on the public internet. That role also carries `storage.objects.list`, so you did not need the URL to find them.

Measured by real set difference against the `AdminIndex` PROJECT partition, not by comparing totals:

| Stage | Thumbnail prefixes | Live projects | Orphaned prefixes | Objects | Size |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| dev | 56 | 49 | **36** | 3,520 | 474 MB |
| prod | 46 | 78 | **5** | **234** | 81 MB |

Prod is exactly why comparing totals fails: fewer thumbnail prefixes than projects, and still orphans.

**Closed in three pieces.** A bucket-level custom role `cdnThumbnailReaper` (`storage.objects.list` + `get` + `delete`) bound to `kindred-reels-gcs@` on both CDN buckets; the fourth sweep back in `services/projectDeletion.js` with its test assertion flipped from negative to positive; and `cleanupOrphanedThumbnails.js` to clean what was already there, run on both stages and re-verified at zero.

`roles/storage.objectAdmin` would have been consistent with the photos and videos buckets, but it also grants create and update, which the backend never needs here (Cloud Run writes the thumbnails). On a public-read bucket that would let a compromised backend serve arbitrary content from `cdn.kindredreels.com`. Reasoning recorded in `docs/INFRASTRUCTURE.md`.

Verified independently after the cleanup: a formerly-public prod frame now returns 404 anonymously, anonymous listing of that prefix is empty, and a live project's thumbnail still returns 200.

### The cleanup script

`backend/src/scripts/cleanupOrphanedThumbnails.js`. Dry run by default, `--stage` required and authoritative, and it always prints and saves a full per-object manifest to `reports/2026-09-12-thumbnail-orphans/<stage>-manifest.txt` before deleting anything. Guard rails, all deliberate: only prefixes absent from the live set are touched, never by age or pattern; a prefix that is not a 32-hex project id aborts the run; and a live-project query returning zero rows aborts, since that would mark the whole bucket orphaned.

**Not verified:** the deployed sweep itself. It cannot be exercised locally (see below) and no deploy was made, so it stays unproven until a real project with a rendered video is deleted on dev.

## setState timers, the whole class

`PhotoUpload.tsx` was one instance of about twenty. In the app these are an invisible wasted render; in tests each is a coin-flip that fails the *entire* suite with an unhandled `window is not defined` after jsdom teardown, while every individual test still passes. `ci.yml` now gates merges on that suite.

**Fixed (14):** the "Copied!" flash in `ShareLinkModal`, `SharePhotosModal`, `ShareVideoModal`, `InviteToAddPhotosModal`, `InviteToRecordModal` and `YouTubeUploadPanel`; the self-re-arming poll loops in `AddPhotosModal` and `AdminFunnel`; the `window.close()` timers in `GooglePhotosCallback` and `YouTubeCallback`; the refetch timers in `AdminSystem`; the scroll timer in `PhotoGallery`; the orientation timer in `useViewportHeight`; and the drag auto-expand in `useTimelineV2Drag`.

**Skipped, and why:**

- `HelpPopover.tsx` and `GooglePhotosPickerStep.tsx` already clear their timers in an effect cleanup.
- `TimelineV2LeftGrid.tsx` has no timer at all; the only `setTimeout(` match is inside a comment.
- `InviteContributorModal.tsx` is unreachable dead UI, mounted in `ProjectLayout` with nothing setting `showInviteModal`. The live surface is `InviteToAddPhotosModal`. Worth deleting, but not here. Already noted in PARKING_LOT #35.

One thing worth knowing: `AddPhotosModal` already had a `mounted` guard, and that is not sufficient. It stops the `setState` but still leaves a pending timer that fires a fetch after teardown.

**Tests.** Four, on the modal group and both hooks, asserting the pending timer count immediately after unmount rather than advancing fake timers first. Each was verified to fail without its fix by breaking the fix and confirming the assertion reads `expected 1 to be +0`.

## Node v22.23.0 breaks authenticated GCS, and it is not the VPN

Every GCS call needing an OAuth token failed with `Premature close` from the token endpoint. It is a Node patch regression, not our code. `@google-cloud/storage` 7.19.0 reaches `node-fetch@2` through a nested `google-auth-library@9.15.1` and `gaxios@6.7.1`, and on v22.23.0 `node-fetch@2` fails on any response sent chunked with no `Content-Length`, which is exactly how Google's token endpoint replies.

| Node | chunked | gzip + Content-Length | token endpoint |
|---|---|---|---|
| v18.20.8 | pass | pass | pass |
| v22.5.1 | pass | pass | pass |
| v22.22.0 | pass | pass | pass |
| **v22.23.0** | **fail** | pass | **fail** |
| v24.13.0 | pass | pass | pass |

Bare native `fetch` to the same URL succeeds, which is why the V4 signed-URL paths (which sign locally and fetch no token) never showed it. Fix is `nvm use 22.22.0`. No code changed; documented under Gotchas in `docs/LOCAL_SETUP.md`.

Lambda runs `nodejs22.x` (`nodejs:22.mainline.v98`) and shows no such errors in its logs, but its exact patch cannot be read from outside and the `gcsObjectExists` path has not run recently (no stale pending uploads), so `sweepStuckVideos` is unremarkable rather than positively cleared.

## New: PARKING_LOT #40, CDN buckets are anonymously listable

Investigated only, no IAM changed, as asked. Both CDN buckets and `cdn.kindredreels.com` itself enumerate without credentials, the branded domain via the S3-compatible XML API through the load balancer. Nothing lists a CDN bucket at runtime: Cloud Run only writes, the frontend builds direct object URLs, the renderer never touches it, and the backend's own listing is authenticated.

The narrowing is smaller than expected and needs no custom role: `roles/storage.legacyObjectReader` is a stock predefined role holding exactly `storage.objects.get`. Left as a decision because the prod bucket sits behind a load balancer with Cloud CDN and getting it wrong breaks every thumbnail in the player.

## Checks

Full pre-push checklist green: backend import check, lint, 1,682 tests; frontend lint, 1,392 tests, build; `processing` 221 tests. Plus **8 consecutive frontend runs, 8/8**, twice (once after a formatting tidy-up), because this bug class does not show up in a single run.

The browser smoke suite was not run: it needs the `E2E_USER_PASSWORD` GitHub secret, which is not available here.

## Docs

`progress.md`, `PARKING_LOT.md` (#39 closed, #40 opened), `INFRASTRUCTURE.md` (the IAM change and its reasoning), `OPERATIONS.md` (script inventory), `LOCAL_SETUP.md` (the Node gotcha), `FRONTEND.md` (the detection heuristic and its false positives), and `INDEX.md` with `Last verified` bumped on each.

Closes parking lot #32, #35 and #36; closes #34 as won't-do; rewrites #33;
opens #39 for the one leak that could not be fixed in code.

#32, the delete cascade. Deleting a project removed its DynamoDB records and
S3 objects and left every photo and clip in GCS. The cause was duplication:
deleteProjectHandler and the admin user-deletion loop each carried a
near-verbatim cascade, and deletePhotoHandler carried a third version of the
per-item half. Only the smallest knew about GCS, so the two that mattered
skipped it. Nobody decided that; it fell out of the copies.

Now one implementation. services/projectDeletion.js holds the cascade and
services/mediaAssets.js the per-item half, with all three callers using them.
The split between those two files is not cosmetic: importing the full cascade
into photoHandler dragged db/videos.js and its db/photos.js import into that
module's graph and broke a test whose mock lacked VIDEO_PENDING_GSI_PK, which
is the trap db/projectCounters.js already documents.

Two more leaks went with it: EMBEDDING# rows, written at upload time for every
item and deleted by nothing, and VIDEO_SHARE# lookup rows, which live under
their own partition key and so outlived their project, leaving a dead
/watch/<code> resolvable. New deleteGcsPrefix sweeps three prefixes across two
GCS buckets, because Cloud Run writes extracted frames to paths no record
stores as a deletable field. The cascade had no tests at all; it now has 16.

#39, opened. Verified against live dev with gcloud rather than trusting logs:
photos/, videos/ and frames/ all went to zero objects for a deleted project,
thumbnails/ kept 4. Cloud Run writes CDN thumbnails under its own identity and
the backend service account has no IAM binding on that bucket, so the fourth
sweep would 403 forever. Omitted deliberately, with a comment and a test
assertion pinning the omission. Needs an IAM grant in both GCP projects.

#36, CI before a merge. Every other workflow runs tests on the way to a
deploy, so they gate the deploy, after the merge, never the merge itself.
ci.yml runs on PRs into main and on pushes to any branch but main, in three
parallel jobs mirroring the pre-push checklist. No cloud credentials, deploys
nothing, and does not run the browser smoke suite.

Adding it exposed a flake that would have made the gate worthless: the
frontend suite was failing about half of all runs with every test passing, on
an unhandled "window is not defined" from React's scheduler after the jsdom
environment was torn down. PhotoUpload.tsx arms three cosmetic setState timers
and cleared none on unmount. Fixed with a ref for the third and one cleanup
for all three; 8 consecutive runs now clean.

#35, 324 skipped tests deleted rather than restored. They asserted against
components since rewritten, and a padded count is worse than a smaller honest
one. The frontend suite is now 1,387 tests with zero skipped.

Four loose ends from the delete-cascade work. One was a disclosure, not
housekeeping.

CDN thumbnails (PARKING_LOT #39, closed). Cloud Run writes thumbnails to
thumbnails/<projectId>/<videoId>/ in the CDN bucket under its own identity, and
the delete cascade never swept that prefix because the backend service account
had no binding on either CDN bucket. Both buckets grant allUsers objectViewer,
so a thumbnail outliving its project stays readable on the public internet, and
since that role also carries storage.objects.list you did not need the URL to
find it.

Measured by real set difference against the AdminIndex PROJECT partition, not by
comparing totals: prod 5 orphaned prefixes / 234 objects / 81 MB, dev 36 / 3,520
/ 474 MB. Prod is why comparing totals fails, it has fewer thumbnail prefixes
(46) than live projects (78) and still had orphans.

Closed with a bucket-level custom role, cdnThumbnailReaper (objects list, get,
delete), bound to kindred-reels-gcs@ on both CDN buckets. objectAdmin would have
matched the photos and videos buckets but also grants write, and write on a
public-read bucket means a compromised backend could serve anything from
cdn.kindredreels.com. The fourth sweep is back in projectDeletion.js and its test
assertion is now positive. cleanupOrphanedThumbnails.js cleaned the existing
orphans on both stages, both re-verified at zero; a formerly-public prod frame
now 404s anonymously and a live project's thumbnail still serves 200.

The script is dry-run by default, requires --stage, and always writes a full
per-object manifest before deleting. It aborts on zero live projects or any
prefix that is not a 32-hex project id, which are the two ways this kind of
script empties a bucket.

setState timers. PhotoUpload was one instance of about twenty. Fourteen were
real and are fixed: the "Copied!" flash in every share modal, two self-re-arming
poll loops, the two OAuth popup callbacks that reach for window, the admin
refetch timers, and the timeline drag auto-expand. Four were correctly left
alone and the reasons are in FRONTEND.md. A mounted flag turned out not to be
enough on its own, it stops the setState but leaves the timer pending. Four
regression tests, each verified to fail without its fix.

Node v22.23.0 breaks every authenticated GCS call, and it is not the VPN. It is
a Node patch regression: @google-cloud/storage reaches node-fetch@2 through a

exactly how Google's token endpoint replies. v18.20.8, v22.5.1, v22.22.0 and

body:
Follow-on from #203. Verifying that fix on prod turned up a retry storm; pulling the thread found three more defects.

## What was happening on prod

Two Cloud Tasks had been retrying for over a day against a project deleted the day before, at attempts **42 and 43 of a possible 100**. Every attempt re-downloaded the source, re-uploaded thumbnails and frames to a world-readable bucket, and paid for a Gemini clip analysis before dying. **85 paid analyses for two videos that were never going to succeed.**

The trigger is an OOM, not a callback failure:

```
Memory limit of 8192 MiB exceeded with 8409 MiB used
```

Cloud Run kills the container, so the task is never a 2xx, so Cloud Tasks retries. Forever, near enough.

Both tasks are deleted and both queues are empty. That was done before anything else.

## Three separate defects, three fixes

### 1. The worker did work nobody wanted

`process_video` now checks the source object still exists before anything expensive, and the endpoint answers `200 {"processed": false, "skipped": "source_missing"}`. A missing source means the project or the video was deleted, so the job is obsolete. Reporting obsolescence as an error is precisely what makes Cloud Tasks retry it.

**Why guard in the worker rather than cancel tasks on delete.** I considered cancelling a project's queued tasks as part of the delete cascade and rejected it:

- It cannot catch a task that is already dispatched. The guard can.
- It only covers project deletion. The guard also covers a deleted video, a failed upload cleanup, and anything else that removes the source.
- Cancelling by name needs deterministic task names, and Cloud Tasks tombstones a name for about an hour after deletion, so re-uploading the same video inside that window would fail to enqueue. That is a real user-facing regression traded for a marginal saving.
- The alternative, listing the queue to find matching tasks, has no payload filter and is racy.

The guard costs one existence check and removes the whole class. A video record that outlives its source is already owned by `sweepStuckVideos`, which makes the same check and then recovers or deletes the record, so the two agree by construction.

### 2. The queue outranked the application

`sweepStuckVideos` re-dispatches a pending video up to `MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3` and then marks it failed. The queues were set to `maxAttempts: 100` with a 0.1s backoff floor. The queue disagreeing with the application by a factor of 33 is what turned one OOM into 85 paid analyses.

Both queues are now **3 attempts, 60s min backoff, 3600s max, 4 doublings**. That keeps a genuine transient failure recoverable and bounds a permanent one. These queues are not IaC-managed, so the settings and the re-apply command are recorded in `docs/INFRASTRUCTURE.md`.

### 3. The frames sweep had never worked

Cloud Run writes storyboard frames to `gs://<CDN bucket>/frames/<projectId>/<videoId>/`, right next to the thumbnails. The delete cascade swept `frames/` from the **videos** bucket, where that prefix has never existed:

```
$ gcloud storage ls gs://kindred-reels-videos-prod/frames/
ERROR: One or more URLs matched no objects.

$ gcloud storage ls gs://kindred-reels-cdn-prod/frames/ | wc -l
47
```

So the sweep matched nothing on every delete since it was written, and every deleted project left its extracted frames publicly readable. Same disclosure as the thumbnails in #203, and larger.

`docs/VIDEO_RENDERING.md` had it documented correctly all along. The code and its test shared the same wrong idea, which is exactly why the test passed. The assertion now pins the bucket, and I verified it fails against the old code.

## Also fixed

**The Lambda role could not list S3.** Both S3 prefix sweeps failed with AccessDenied on every project delete, and had done since they were written. `s3:ListBucket` is a bucket-level action taking the bare bucket ARN with no `/*`, and the role had only object-level grants. The videos bucket also had no `s3:DeleteObject` at all, so nothing could ever remove a rendered reel.

This is the one change that touches `serverless.yml`, which CLAUDE.md normally puts off limits. There is nowhere else the Lambda role can be fixed. **It reaches a stage only on that stage's next backend deploy.**

**The prod smoke suite could never have passed.** `blockAnalytics` used `route.abort()`, and an aborted request makes Chromium log `Failed to load resource: net::ERR_FAILED`, which F1's zero-console-errors assertion caught. Dev never hit it because `deploy-frontend.yml` builds dev with an empty `VITE_GA_MEASUREMENT_ID`, so the app never requests gtag there and there is nothing to abort. The first ever prod run hit it immediately.

The helper now fulfils those routes with an empty 200. Nothing reaches Google either way, and the console assertion stays strict rather than growing a host allowlist that could hide a real error later.

## Cleanup: both stages, manifest before deletion as always

`cleanupOrphanedThumbnails.js` is now `cleanupOrphanedCdnMedia.js` and reaps both roots. A cleanup script that covers one of two identical leaks is a trap, and the old name asserted a coverage it no longer had.

| Stage | Orphaned prefixes | Objects | Size |
|---|---|---|---|
| dev | 37 | 11,925 | 125 MB |
| prod | 6 | 636 | 20 MB |

That is on top of the thumbnails cleared in #203. Both stages re-verified at zero afterwards, and the thumbnail and frame prefix counts now match exactly, 20/20 on dev and 42/42 on prod, which is the consistency check that would have caught this earlier. A formerly-public prod frame returns 404 anonymously.

## The item #203 left open is now closed

The CDN thumbnail sweep works in the deployed Lambda. The dev smoke run's own project, at teardown:

```
🧹 GCS prefix sweep gs://kindred-reels-cdn-dev/thumbnails/f48f3151.../: 2/2 deleted
✅ Successfully deleted project f48f3151... with 2 photos and 0 recordings
```

## Deliberately not fixed, both written up

- **PARKING_LOT #41, the OOM.** 8Gi exceeded on a 31.6 MB source, which suggests a leak rather than a genuine requirement. Bounded now by the retry ceiling, so that clip fails three times instead of a hundred, but it still cannot be analysed. Profiling it is its own piece of work, and the same service has a separate known OOM in the YouTube path.
- **PARKING_LOT #42, orphaned `EMBEDDING#` rows.** One deleted prod project still carries 505 of them. There is no set-difference route here the way there is for a bucket, since you cannot enumerate `PROJECT#*` partitions by prefix, so finding them means a full table scan. I rejected the tempting shortcut of reusing the CDN cleanup's known-deleted ids: it would only find projects that also left CDN media behind, so it would report success while missing every deleted project that had no video. A cleanup that silently covers a subset is worse than none, because it stops anyone looking.

## Checks

Backend import check, lint, 1,682 tests. Frontend lint, 1,392 tests, build. Processing 221 tests. Plus **8 consecutive frontend runs, 8/8**.

Docs: `progress.md`, `PARKING_LOT.md` (#41, #42), `INFRASTRUCTURE.md` (queue retry config, S3 IAM, CDN bucket contents), `VIDEO_RENDERING.md` (the guard), `OPERATIONS.md` (renamed script), `LOCAL_SETUP.md`, and `INDEX.md` with `Last verified` bumped.

## Note on merging

This touches `services/video-processor/**`, so merging also fires `deploy-cloud-run.yml` to dev, which has **no lint or test gate**. And the `serverless.yml` IAM fix needs a backend deploy per stage, so prod S3 sweeps stay broken until the next release tag.

body:
All three were parked as "correct but bigger than the change in hand". Two turned out smaller than the write-ups feared, and one was a different bug than its title said.

## #40: the CDN buckets were anonymously listable

`allUsers` held `roles/storage.objectViewer`, which carries `storage.objects.list` as well as `get`. Both buckets enumerated without credentials, and so did `cdn.kindredreels.com`, because the load balancer passes the S3-compatible XML list API straight through to the bucket. That is what turned #39 from litter into a disclosure: you could find a deleted project's frames without knowing any URL.

Swapped to `roles/storage.legacyObjectReader`, a stock predefined role holding exactly `storage.objects.get`. No custom role needed.

Dev first, then prod, verified at each step:

| Check | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| JSON list API, anonymous | 200 | **401** |
| XML list API via `cdn.kindredreels.com` | 200 | **403** |
| Object GET, direct | 200 | 200 |
| Object GET via load balancer, **cache-busted** | 200 | 200 |
| Landing sample video | 200 | 200 |
| Backend authenticated listing | works | works |

The cache-busted request is the one that carries the information. A cached object would have served either way, so without busting the cache the check proves nothing. Also confirmed the backend still lists through `cdnThumbnailReaper`, which is what the delete cascade depends on.

## #41: not a memory leak, an 8K video

The clip that OOM'd the 8Gi container is **7680x4320 HEVC**, 33 megapixels a frame, and 2.9 seconds long. It died in the transcode, where ffmpeg ran with default thread counts and every thread holds its own full-resolution frame buffers.

The renderer's largest output is 4K (`processing/src/video/models.py`), so an 8K intermediate bought nothing at all. Capped the scale at 3840x2160 and pinned the threads. Measured on a reproduction of the failing input:

| Configuration | Peak RSS | Time |
|---|---|---|
| No cap, default threads (what shipped) | 3.51 GiB | 8.87s |
| 4K cap, encode threads 4 | 2.39 GiB | 2.30s |
| 4K cap, decode + encode threads 4 | 1.89 GiB | 2.32s |
| **4K cap, decode + encode threads 2** | **1.27 GiB** | **2.29s** |

**64% less memory, 3.9x faster**, output correctly 3840x2160 H.264.

Bounding the **decoder** is what did most of the work, and it is easy to miss: `-threads` placed after `-i` only reaches the encoder. Two threads cost nothing in wall time even at the worst supported input, a 120s 4K source, which measured 1.01 GiB / 68.8s against 1.20 GiB / 69.1s at four. Well inside the 600s timeout.

Two edge cases checked rather than assumed, because a scale filter is easy to get subtly wrong:

- A **640x480** input stays 640x480. The filter uses `min()` against the source, so it never upscales. A plain `force_original_aspect_ratio=decrease` on a 3840x2160 box would have blown every phone clip up to 4K, making things worse rather than better.
- A **1081x721** input comes out 1080x720, via `force_divisible_by=2`, since libx264 requires even dimensions.

The retry ceiling of 3 from the previous PR stays, so a future deterministic failure is still bounded whatever causes it.

## #42: wider than its title

Filed as orphaned `EMBEDDING#` rows. The actual bug is that a project **partition** outlived its project, so every row type in it is equally stranded. Reaping only the type that happened to get noticed would have left the rest behind and stopped anyone looking, so `cleanupOrphanedProjectRows.js` deletes the whole orphaned partition and reports the breakdown.

| Stage | Partitions | Rows | Types |
|---|---|---|---|
| dev | 176 | **7,715** | 14 types: EMBEDDING# 5,998, MEMORY# 812, PHOTO# 555, SECTION# 163, VIDEO# 51, PERSON# 34, VIDEO_CONTENT# 32, SHARE# 30, and 6 more |
| prod | 7 | **785** | 5 types: EMBEDDING# 764, VIDEO_CONTENT# 14, USER_PREFS# 4, SECTION# 2, RESTORATION_JOB# 1 |

Both re-verified at zero. Dev went from 229 `PROJECT#` partitions to 49, matching its 49 live projects exactly.

The scan the write-up worried about was a non-issue. Both tables are 22k to 27k items, a few seconds each, and the scan projects PK and SK only, which matters: embedding rows carry 1408-dimension vectors and pulling those would have made a cheap job an expensive one.

The orphan test requires **two independent signals**: no `METADATA` row AND absent from the AdminIndex live set. Either alone can be wrong. An index gap would make a live project look dead; a half-finished delete could leave `METADATA` behind.

### Two guard rails earned their keep

**The dev run refused to start.** It found four partitions whose ids are not project ids: `PROJECT#undefined` (two PHOTO rows from 2025-12-28, every field undefined), `PROJECT#project-123` (the frontend test fixture id, with an all-undefined METADATA row), plus two more test ids. Nine-month-old debris written into the real dev table, from before it was understood that local runs write live dev data. I deleted those five rows by explicit key as a one-off rather than loosening the guard, which was right to stop and should stay strict.

**The first prod delete threw `ProvisionedThroughputExceededException` after 733 rows.** Every row in an orphaned partition shares one PK, so a large partition is by definition a hot key while it is being deleted, and on-demand capacity scales but not instantly. My script handled `UnprocessedItems` but not a *thrown* throttle, which are two different failure shapes and missing either one loses rows. It now handles both, paces batches, and is idempotent, so the re-run picked up the remaining 52.

## Checks

Backend import check, lint, 1,682 tests. Frontend lint, 1,392 tests, build. Processing 221 tests. Plus 8 consecutive frontend runs, 8/8.

Docs: `PARKING_LOT.md` (#40, #41, #42 all closed with their measurements), `INFRASTRUCTURE.md`, `VIDEO_RENDERING.md`, `OPERATIONS.md`, `progress.md`, `INDEX.md`.

## Note on deploying

The #40 IAM change and both cleanups are **already applied to live infrastructure**; they are not waiting on this merge. What the merge ships is the transcode fix, which reaches dev via `deploy-cloud-run.yml` (no test gate) and prod on the next release tag. Until then the 8K clip still OOMs on prod, bounded to 3 attempts.

body:
The pre-push hook caught an unhandled error from `DraftMemoryModal`. All 1,392 tests passed. The error came from a promise resolving after the test environment had already shut down.

## The bug

The code saved a recording, closed the modal, then set state on the modal it had just closed:

```js
onSuccess();
onClose();                 // unmounts
} finally {
  setIsUploading(false);   // runs afterwards
}
```

Nine instances across five files, found by looking for a `finally` that sets state inside a handler whose `try` calls `onClose`, `onSuccess` or `navigate`:

| File | Handlers |
|---|---|
| `MemoryModal.tsx` | remove photo, ungroup, move to video, recording complete |
| `DraftMemoryModal.tsx` | recording complete, remove photo, ungroup |
| `AddPhotosToMemoryModal.tsx` | add photos |
| `NewProject.tsx` | create project |
| `ContributeBrowse.tsx` | validate share code |

Where the handler always closes, the reset moved into `catch`, the only path where the component is still on screen. That is what the code meant all along: if we are leaving, there is no flag left to reset.

Three need a local flag instead. Removing the last photo dissolves the memory and closes, but removing any other photo leaves the modal open (two of these). And `ContributeBrowse` navigates from inside the `try` and then returns, which does **not** skip the `finally`.

`RotateControls` matches the shape and is **not** a bug. Its `onSuccess` refreshes the photo but leaves the control on screen, so resetting its flag is correct. I checked each match rather than mass-editing.

## Why the earlier sweep missed this

This is the same class as the setState-timer work the day before, reached a different way. That sweep counted `setTimeout` against `clearTimeout`. Here there is no timer at all, just an async continuation resuming after the component is gone, so that heuristic structurally could not find it. Both shapes are now written up in `docs/FRONTEND.md` with the detection method and the false positives for each.

## What is not proven, plainly

**With the bug deliberately put back, it would not reproduce: 0 in 35 runs.** It needs the full suite running in parallel and the right timing. So the ten clean runs afterwards are consistent with a fix but do not demonstrate one.

What is certain is narrower and still worth having: the crash came from one specific line running after teardown, and that line no longer runs on the path that closes the modal. The reported failure cannot recur.

## Two new CLAUDE.md rules

**"You Wrote All Of This Code."** Never frame a defect as pre-existing, someone else's, or not from this session. There is one developer on this project. When a bug appeared is worth saying only when it helps: it points at the cause, it bounds how much data needs cleaning, or it informs priority. Never as a reason the bug matters less.

**"Write Plainly."** Ordinary words, short sentences, explain the thing rather than naming it.

## Beta launch tracker, caught up

- **Bucket 15 (testing pyramid) closed.** Every item done, the last being the smoke suite green against prod, 11/11. I verified the funnel-exclusion prereq rather than assuming it, because snapshots are immutable and a gap would permanently pollute the beta numbers. The live prod Lambda logged 23 excluded user ids before the first successful prod run, so the metrics are clean.
- **Buckets 4, 5 and 9** get done items and archive pointers, not status changes, since none of their recon has happened. Bucket 9's "verify a data deletion path exists" item now has a different answer than when it was written.
- **Bucket 12** had a pre-existing inconsistency: its summary row said IN PROGRESS while its section and both phases said DONE. Corrected, since the tracker's own rule 4 requires them to match.
- **Target launch window** moved to end of September 2026.

Detail went to `TRACKER_ARCHIVE.md` per the tracker's maintenance rules, with new sections for buckets 4, 9 and 15.

## Checks

Frontend lint, typecheck, build, and 1,392 tests over 10 consecutive runs with no unhandled errors. The pre-push hook, which is what caught this, passes.

Closes bucket 1 of the beta launch tracker: the eight items from the watched session with Joe.

Six were one or two files each and landed earlier. This describes the three that needed a plan first. The plan and its post-mortem are committed at `.claude/plans/bucket1-joe-batch.md`.

## F. Check the rebuild limit before it is too late to matter

A project gets ten timeline rebuilds, and the check for that lived in the organize endpoint. Analysis runs first, and its worker opens by deleting rejected clip stubs and clearing timeline-derived `ai_metadata` on every photo. So a project at the cap lost its Not Included column, spent a full analysis pass of Gemini calls, and was then told it had never been allowed to rebuild.

The check now runs in `analyzeEventHandler` too, before the draft is created and before the worker is dispatched. It reads `req.project`, which ownership middleware has already loaded, so it costs no extra read. Only organize increments, so gating analyze cannot double-count.

The limit was also invisible until you hit it. GET project now returns `organizeRebuildCount` and `organizeRebuildLimit`. Both, not just the count: the limit is the incident tuning surface, so a frontend hardcoding 10 would keep promising ten after someone lowered it. At the cap the confirm button is removed rather than disabled, so the destructive path is unreachable from the UI.

## C. Let a video skip the section title cards

A new project field, `sectionCardsEnabled`, shown in Settings and in Create Video, honored by the renderer. Off gives one continuous slideshow; sections still set item order and where the music changes.

The renderer was built for this, so its change is one thing: `build_section_ordered_items` skips both `section_title` inserts. Section boundaries come from each item's `section_id`, never from a card.

The trap the spec missed is the music timeline. `getSlideDurations` opens every section's duration with the card's duration and the picker places music against those durations, so with the cards off every section would read eight seconds longer than it is. It now returns zero for the card. The Create Video runtime estimate drops the same term.

The default is on, which makes `||` wrong at every read site: `stored || true` can never be false. Every site uses `??` in JS and `settings.get(key, DEFAULT)` in Python, with a test at each one that stores false and reads it back.

**New: `shared/constants.json`.** The default lives in one file, and `node scripts/generate-shared-constants.js` emits a native module for each stack. Generated rather than imported, because Python cannot import JS, Vite would need `server.fs.allow` widened past the frontend root, and the renderer's Docker image only copies `processing/`. Nothing forces the generator to be re-run, so each stack has a test that reads the JSON and fails if its committed module disagrees. All three were confirmed to fail on a drifted value and pass when current.

## B. Say when a cover photo has no preview

Joe reported the cover thumbnail looking broken. The plan blamed the two consumers preferring opposite fields. Scanning both stages killed that theory: across 5,893 dev photos and 11,562 prod photos there is not one case where the two disagree about whether the image loads.

It was a video clip. A clip has no `storagePath` and no `thumbnailStoragePath`, so `cdn_thumbnail_url` is its only image, and 110 of dev's 466 timeline clips point at `cdn.kindredreels.com`. That host fronts the PROD bucket and nothing else, so a dev record holding it asks prod for an object that only exists in dev. Prod has 13. Reproduced in Chrome: 29 broken images on one dev project's timeline page, 10 of 22 selectable cover tiles blank.

Nothing checked whether the cover loaded. Three surfaces drew it, none had an `onError`, and one draws it inside a sandboxed iframe where a 404 is completely silent. Now a failed tile reads "No preview", the previews show a placeholder and a sentence, and whichever surface finds out first tells the others, which is the only way that iframe can ever know.

`isCurrentFrameUrl` widens the clip-boundary self-repair so a wrong-host URL heals the next time anyone edits the clip. The old repair only looked for a misspelled frame name or a frame outside the trim, and these URLs pass both.

**The copy was corrected before shipping.** The first draft said the video would pick a different cover. That is false: the renderer resolves the cover from the photo's S3 object, or by extracting its own frame from the clip's source video with ffmpeg, and never reads these thumbnails. The finished video is right either way. A test asserts on that distinction.

Existing broken clips are not backfilled, by decision. The config that wrote them is already correct on both stages and dev is reimported constantly.

## Verification

Checked in Chrome on real data, not only in tests: the cards toggle saves and survives a reload, the Section titles duration row dims, the runtime estimate moves by the card duration per section, and the music timeline total drops by the same amount on the same page. For B, the broken tiles now read "No preview" and the theme iframe stops receiving the dead URL.

Not verified: no video has been rendered with the cards off. Everything up to the job payload is checked; the render itself needs the EC2 renderer.

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| Backend | 1,716 passing |
| Frontend | 1,449 passing |
| Processing | 232 passing |
| Lint | 0 errors, 0 warnings both sides |
| Build | clean |

## What merging triggers

Per the workflow table in `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md`: this branch touches `backend/**`, `frontend/**` and `processing/**`, so merging to main starts **three** DEV deploys, not one.

- `deploy-backend.yml` → Lambda dev
- `deploy-frontend.yml` → S3 sync + CloudFront invalidation
- `deploy-processing.yml` → EC2 renderer dev, **and it starts the instance if it is stopped**

`deploy-cloud-run.yml` does not fire; `services/video-processor/**` is untouched.

## Logged, not fixed

In bucket 14: four timeline surfaces that still draw a dead thumbnail with no fallback, prod's 13 wrong-host clips, the drifted slide-duration constants (`GenerateVideoModal` estimates with 5/5/7 while the backend sends 8/8/15), the renderer's face backfill writing `face_data` where the backend reads `faceData`, and no cache invalidation when a render completes.

backend already resolves request.settings.themeId > project.selectedThemeId >
default, so the picked theme reached the job it was picked for and then

the theme card swaps in place.

A failed write is not worth a toast. The render still uses the picked theme
and the only cost is the next prefill, so it logs and moves on rather than
interrupting someone mid-flow who has lost nothing.

The title has been editable from the timeline since the overhaul. The
subtitle sat behind the kebab menu and the Section Settings modal for no
reason anyone could name, so changing one word meant opening a dialog.

Mirrors the title exactly: isEditing/editValue, pencil on hover, Enter or
blur commits, Escape discards, optimistic cache write with rollback through
the same updateSection the modal calls. Both paths stay interchangeable.

Two differences, both deliberate. An empty subtitle is a legitimate value,
since clearing it is how you remove one, so commitSubtitle saves the empty
string rather than treating it as a cancel the way the title does. And the
subtitle moved to its own line under the title instead of sharing the flex
row: a long subtitle was eating the title's truncate budget, and an absent
one left nowhere to hang an affordance. With no subtitle, a muted "Add
subtitle" appears on hover and is itself the target.

layout. Existing callers that pass a position class to Tooltip are suspect
for the same reason; noted in bucket 14.
