Section title cards (the short card that names each section) are now off by default for every project, and the setting's description says what turning them on adds. Before flipping the default, this fixes the bug that would have made it wrong for many videos: with cards off, photos in a post-credits section played before the credits.

## What changes for people

- **Default off.** Projects that never touched the setting render as one continuous slideshow, with no dividers. Projects where someone set it keep their choice.
- **New wording:** "Show a title card at the start of each section" / "Adds a short card with the section's name before each part of the video, like chapters. Leave it off for one continuous slideshow."
- **Post-credits placement (#76).** The renderer and both timeline builders used to spot post-credits items by the section's title-card marker, which does not exist with cards off. Now an item counts as post-credits when its own section is a post-credits section, through one function, `post_credits_flags` in `timeline.py`.

## Found and fixed along the way

- The final mix lost each section's music volume and keep-loud setting when cards were off. It now gets the full section list.
- A run of crossfaded photos could carry on across the credits into the post-credits photos. It is now broken at that point.
- A log line and a comment claimed post-credits sections had a title card. They never did.

With cards on, output is unchanged. An independent review ran the same scenario on main and on this branch and got identical timelines, to the millisecond.

Also recorded, not fixed here: parking lot #105. By reading the code, the music picker appears to count post-credits photos toward the first section. It needs reproducing first.

## After merge (dev deploys renderer, backend and frontend)

Render a dev project with two or more normal sections and one post-credits section with a few photos, with the section-cards box unchecked. Check that there are no title cards, that the post-credits photos come after the credits, and that their music starts right after the credits.

Checks: backend 2,673 tests pass; frontend 1,638 tests pass, and lint and the build are clean; processing 313 tests pass.

body:
Two tier 1 items came from how CI deploys. It signed in to AWS with the founder's personal administrator key (#89). It copied renderer code to the EC2 machine over SSH, which kept port 22 open to the whole internet (#82). This PR changes the method and keeps the workflow: merging to main still deploys dev, and a release tag still deploys prod.

## What changes

- **One deploy script** for the laptop and CI, `backend/src/scripts/deployRenderer.js`. It packages the renderer and uploads it to S3 under `renderer-deploy/<stage>/` in that stage's videos bucket. It then runs `processing/deploy/install.sh` on the machine through AWS Systems Manager (SSM) Run Command. No SSH and no open port.
- **It restarts the service** (#90). The old laptop deploy ran `start`, which did nothing to a running renderer. The deploy fails if the service does not stay up.
- **Stage safety:** `--stage` is required and checked against the instance id, the instance's Environment tag and the bundle.
- **CI signs in with GitHub OIDC**: short-lived credentials, one role per stage, no stored AWS keys. Every AWS job declares `environment: dev` or `environment: prod`.
- `launchVideoProcessingEC2.js` no longer recreates the open port 22 rule.

## Already done in the cloud (2026-09-24), see `infra/ci/RUNBOOK.md`

- GitHub OIDC provider, and roles `kindred-github-deploy-dev` and `-prod`. The policies are committed in `infra/ci/policies/`. They were checked against two days of real CI calls in CloudTrail, which added read permissions the first draft missed and dropped the Serverless v4 pieces (CI runs v3). Simulated: each role can command only its own machine, and the dev role cannot touch the prod stack or frontend.
- GitHub environments: `dev` accepts `main` only, until the renderer roles are split (#83). `prod` accepts `main` and `v*` tags. The role variables are set.
- Deploy log group `/loomed-memories/renderer-deploy`, kept 30 days.
- **Rehearsal on the real dev machine, from the laptop, with port 22 still open:** it passed first time. The install finished, the service restarted at the deploy time with no restarts after, Python packages are owned by ec2-user, nothing went under /root, and the machine is on the dev queue.

## Merge order

- Merging this switches dev CI straight away. The merge itself redeploys dev backend, frontend and renderer through OIDC and SSM, which is the CI-side proof.
- Prod switches on the next release tag. Before that tag, rehearse a prod deploy from the laptop (runbook step 9).
- After both work: close port 22 on dev, then prod, then delete the SSH and personal-key secrets and rotate the personal key (runbook steps 8 to 12).

One cost, by design: until #83, dev workflows cannot be dispatched from a feature branch. Use the manual dev frontend deploy in DEPLOYMENT.md for that.

Also in this PR: the planned narrow renderer roles (#83) may now write the deploy log group, which the merge review found missing. New parking lot items: #102 (the CI backend role is broad because `serverless deploy` needs it) and #103 (Cloud Run deploys still use a stored GCP key).

Checks: backend 2,697 tests pass, frontend 1,636 tests pass, processing 302 tests pass, and lint and the build are clean.

On the timeline, Add Section and Add Post-Credits Section used to create the section on the server first, then open the settings dialog as an editor for it. So Create stayed greyed out until some field changed (the mood was usually what people touched), and Cancel left the new section behind. Found by Dimitri while testing post-credits on dev.

## What changes

- Both buttons open the settings dialog in a new **create mode**, titled "New Section", with the usual default title filled in ("Section N", "Post-Credits", "Post-Credits 2").
- **Create Section** is enabled whenever the title is not empty. Nothing is sent to the server until you press it.

- Editing an existing section works exactly as before.
- `POST /sections` now accepts `musicVolume`, validated the same way as update, so a volume set in the dialog is kept.

body:
Fixes PARKING_LOT #114. When a section had two songs in a row, an uploaded song that was not the last one vanished from the video: the renderer read a track's length only from `duration` (seconds), which library tracks have, while uploaded tracks store `durationMs`. The length came out as 0 and the mixer skipped the song.

- `processing/src/music_resolver.py`: `track_duration_ms` reads `durationMs` first, then `duration` (the backend's order), for both kinds of track. `fill_missing_durations` measures the downloaded file with ffprobe when neither exists, and logs an error naming the song if even that fails.
- `processing/src/video/audio.py`: `get_audio_duration` returns 0.0 and logs instead of raising on ffprobe `N/A`, a timeout (new 30s limit) or a missing binary, so one unreadable song can only drop itself, never fail the whole render (review finding).
- `processing/src/video/timeline.py`: logs when a song in a chain has no length.
- Tests: 327 processing tests pass; the uploaded-track and mid-chain tests fail on the old code.

Reviewed independently: ship after the ffprobe hardening, which is included. Merging redeploys the dev renderer through CI; prod gets it with the next release. Checklist: backend 2791, frontend 1667, lints clean, build passes.

downloaded file with ffprobe, and an unmeasurable file is logged by name.

body:
The final video used to end on a still "Thanks for watching" card in about 14 seconds of complete silence, because the last song stopped when the last photo ended. Now the credits open on the film's exact last frame, fade it to the theme's color, and the Kindred Reels mark draws itself as two fine lines that glide together, link and fill in, before the usual card (sign-off, contributor names on tributes, wordmark, address) fades up. The last section's song keeps playing under it and fades to silence over the last 3 seconds. Chosen by Dimitri from five prototypes. Plan: `.claude/plans/credits-weave-ending.md`.

**How it renders:** the existing credits HTML template plays the animation frame by frame; the renderer's existing Playwright Chromium screenshots each frame and FFmpeg encodes them. No Remotion, nothing new installed on the render box.

**Behavior**
- Default credits length is 10 s everywhere, from one shared constant (was 15, with a stray 7 in the estimate).
- Credits shorter than 8 s, or any failure in the animated path, render today's still card instead. A crashed or frozen Chromium is relaunched, and every browser and FFmpeg step has a time limit, so a credits problem never fails or hangs a video.

The video analyzer's CI deploy signed in to Google Cloud with `GCP_SA_KEY`, a never-expiring key for an account that can deploy anything in the project. This switches the dev workflow (`deploy-cloud-run.yml`) to Workload Identity Federation, the same pattern the AWS jobs use since #89: GitHub hands the job a short-lived token, and Google trades it for one-hour credentials of a small per-stage deploy account.

**Already applied by hand 2026-09-26:** pool `github` + provider `kindredreels` (only this repo, only the `dev`/`prod` environments); `gha-cloudrun-deploy-{dev,prod}@`, each usable only from its own environment, with service-level grants only; GitHub variables `GCP_WIF_PROVIDER`, `GCP_DEPLOY_SA_DEV`, `GCP_DEPLOY_SA_PROD`. Old account and key untouched.

**Workflow:** runs in the `dev` environment (or the dispatched one), `id-token: write`, WIF auth, deploys with `--service-account video-processor-<stage>@`, drops `--no-allow-unauthenticated` (the new account cannot write service IAM; the service's existing access is unchanged). A guard step refuses to deploy a service not already on its own runtime account, so a prod dispatch stops there until #96 B4.

The video callbacks (render complete/failed from the EC2 renderer, clip analysis from Cloud Run) accepted a per-job signed token or, during the rollout, the old shared password. Both stages have run on tokens for more than 72 quiet hours, so this removes the old password. On the way it fixes the bug behind the one stray password use: a video deleted while its render job was still queued came back as a "ghost" record, and the founder got a failure email for a video that no longer existed.

**Ghost records, fixed everywhere:**
- Renderer: every VIDEO# write only lands on a record that exists. A job whose video is gone is dropped on first receive and its queue message deleted; no callback, no alert. A real failure on an existing video still emails.
- Backend: every update to a VIDEO# record goes through `updateExistingVideo` (`attribute_exists(PK)`): render and YouTube status, the two stuck-job sweeps, share writes. A deleted video means no write, no email, a 404 from the route, and the YouTube worker stops without retry. The failure-email claim also requires `createdAt`.

**Stage 2:** any bearer that is not a valid per-job token gets 401. `callVideoProcessor` and `createVideo` throw if no token can be minted. Nothing reads the old secret. Both signing keys exist (dev 2026-09-24, prod 2026-09-25). Prod: zero legacy callbacks since its key, 51 clip and 7 render callbacks on tokens.

**Parking lot:** #84 updated (closes once the old secrets are deleted); new #137 (finished MP4 left in S3 when a video is deleted mid-render) and #138 (seven old stub records).

**What merging deploys:** `deploy-dev.yml` deploys the renderer, then the backend, to dev. Either order is safe: every job queued since the keys exist carries a token. Prod gets it on the next release tag.

**After the release:** delete `kindred-reels/video-processor-callback-secret-dev` and `-prod` per `docs/runbooks/callback-tokens.md` section 5.

Reviewed twice (ship). Checks: backend `node --check`, lint, 2837 tests; processing 378 tests; frontend lint, 1684 tests, build.

commits.messageBody:
Stage 2 of #84. CALLBACK_AUTH=legacy was silent for more than 72 hours in
both stages, so the old shared callback password is no longer accepted or
sent anywhere. verifyCallbackAuth rejects any non-token bearer as
not_a_token. callVideoProcessor and createVideo now refuse a job when no
token can be minted, because such a job could never call back. The six
clip dispatch sites and the renderer no longer read
video-processor-callback-secret, and the renderer sends no callback at
all for a record without a token. Cloud Run is unchanged: it still echoes
the callbackSecret field, which has carried a token since stage one.

The one legacy callback seen during the quiet window was a bug. A user
deleted a dev render 4 seconds after queueing it. The renderer failed on
the missing record three times, and then the attempt cap wrote a stub
VIDEO# record (update_item creates a missing key) and emailed a failure
alert for a deleted video. Seven such stubs exist in dev and prod, some
"complete" from deletes mid-render. Now:
- the renderer drops a job whose record is gone on the first receive;
- every renderer VIDEO# write is conditional on the record existing, and
  a refused write sends no callback (report_render_failure);
- the backend's updateVideoStatus is conditional too, so the stuck-render
  sweep sends no alert for a video deleted under it;
- claimRenderNotification requires createdAt, so an existing stub can
  never send an email.

body:
A user wrote in on 2026-10-01 that photos stay on screen too long and asked for about one second per photo. There was no way to change that. This PR adds a photo pace setting on each project: Relaxed, Normal (the default, same as today) and Fast. To make the paces line up with the music, it also rewrites how the renderer times photos to music. The old beat timing spaced photos like the music but never actually put the changes on the beat.

## What changes for users
- **Create Video dialog:** a Pace choice. Each option shows its own length estimate, the main estimate updates when the choice changes, and a plain line says the timeline itself doesn't change. The pace is saved to the project as soon as it is picked. Create is blocked until that save succeeds.
- **Music top-up:** if the picked pace makes a section outlast its music, a same-mood track is added to that section and named on screen, with a link that opens that section's music picker. Switching back removes only tracks the pace added. If no matching track is left, a warning appears instead.
- **Every photo change lands on the beat** at every pace, including after clips and where one song hands over to the next.

## Renderer (`processing/`)
- Each photo lasts a whole number of beats (Fast) or bars (Normal, Relaxed). Normal keeps the old rule for choosing the musical unit, so photo lengths match today's videos.
- Fixes #123 (cuts not on the beat) and four bugs that were never in the parking lot:
  - a section with two songs was timed to its last song;
  - a rounding step dropped photos, which then played after the song ended;
  - the end-of-music fade was scheduled after the file ended, so it never played;
  - frame rounding drifted cuts 1 to 6 s late over a long section.
- Photos are never squeezed to fit a song. When they outlast it, the song fades over its last 2 s, then silence.
- A voice recording now turns beat timing off only in its own section, not the whole video.
- Fast gets 0.12 s crossfades and a smaller zoom.
- Measured on all 64 library tracks: Normal picks the same unit as main on every one. On the 5 test tracks, cuts land within 17 ms of a beat.

## Backend and frontend
- New `PROJECT#.photoPace`, validated; the render job uses the saved pace only.
- `PHOTO_PACES` in `shared/constants.json`, generated into all three stacks.
- One shared length estimate. Music is sized with a 1.2x margin in Create Timeline, the pace top-up, the dialog warning and the picker.
- New `PUT /api/projects/:id/photo-pace`.
- Every music placement write bumps `musicPlacementsVersion` and is conditional on it. A conflict returns 409, and the dialog and picker re-read and retry.
- Also fixes #105: post-credits items no longer count toward the first section's music. #69 is half done.

## Checks
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Backend `node --check`, lint | clean, 0 warnings |
| Backend tests | 2909 passed |
| Frontend lint | clean, 0 warnings |
| Frontend tests | 1733 passed |
| Frontend build | succeeds |
| Processing tests | 1169 passed |

Three rounds of independent review, every finding fixed. Founder tested locally: the dialog and a Relaxed render.

## Deploy
Merging deploys the frontend, and the renderer then the backend in that order (`deploy-dev.yml`), to dev. Either order is safe: the renderer ignores keys it doesn't know, and a missing `photoPace` means Normal. No Cloud Run deploy, no `serverless.yml` change, no cloud setup, no data backfill.

New parking lot item #139: a section whose library song was deleted shows a beat-timed estimate but renders at the flat length. This affects the estimate only.

body:
Almost every photo in a video zoomed in by a faint 5% and barely moved toward the face. Gemini's suggested move had not reached the renderer since February, and panning was removed in November 2025 because the old pans did not know where faces were. This PR gives every photo a move chosen from what is in it, with rules picked from side-by-side test renders of a real dev project (Outer Banks 2026).

**The rules** (`processing/src/video/camera.py`, one module for slideshow runs, single photos and recorded memories, replacing three copies that had drifted apart):
- One or two people, faces not tiny: zoom in toward them.
- A group, or people small in the frame: start close on them and pull back.
- No people: pan, sideways on wide photos and up or down on tall ones, ending toward Gemini's subject point. A detail shot zooms in on it instead.
- Zoom 10%. Pans slide 15% of what is on screen, at the same speed for every photo shape. At Fast pace both shrink, as before.
- A face is never cut off, in either the wide or the close framing.
- Never three zooms the same way in a row; moves are decided once over the whole video.

**Backend:** the render job now carries `cameraHints` per photo (Gemini's camera target, its subject point, and its people / place / detail label, all already stored on every photo) instead of `aiMetadata`, which was always empty. Gemini's own suggested move is no longer used. Faces the renderer detects during a render now reach single photos in that same render.

**Checked:**
- The 12 test photos rendered through the new production code match the approved test render frame for frame.
- An independent review found nothing blocking; its fixes (pan speed on tall and very wide photos, two doc lines, a test for recorded memories) are in.
- Founder watched a full local render.
- Backend lint and 2,929 tests, frontend lint, 1,762 tests and build, renderer 1,240 tests (52 new for the camera, which had no tests before).

**Deploy:** merging deploys the renderer and then the backend to dev (`deploy-dev.yml`). Either order is safe: a new renderer with an old job just pans photos without people around the centre, and an old renderer ignores the new field. No frontend, Cloud Run, `serverless.yml` or data changes. Prod gets it with the next release tag.

**Docs:** VIDEO_RENDERING 2.1, 2.7, 2.9; PIPELINES; ai-inventory; progress. Parking lot: #124 closed (its write-up was partly wrong, corrected in the Closed row), #109 closed without running the repair script, new #140 for five unanswered prod feedback messages.

body:
Every voice recording in a rendered video had audible static. The renderer puts one second of silence before each recording by joining a silent clip from ffmpeg's `anullsrc` to the voice. On FFmpeg 8 that silent clip is 8-bit audio, and the join converts both clips to one format, so the whole voice was cut down to 8 bits. It is then saved as 16-bit again, which hid it until the audio was measured step by step. Older FFmpeg builds produced 16-bit silence, which is why a January render sounded fine.

The fix starts the voice one second late with `adelay` instead (one input, so nothing has to agree on a format). Both lead-in sites in `segments.py` now call one helper, `prepend_lead_in` in `video/audio.py`.

**How it was found and checked**
- On a real render's kept temp files, energy at 12-16 kHz relative to the voice went from -75 dB before the lead-in to -39 dB after it. With the fix it stays at -75 dB on all three recordings.
- A full local render of the tribute sample video with this branch: all three voices present, no static (checked by ear).

**Tests**
- New `processing/tests/test_voice_lead_in.py` (5 tests, real FFmpeg on a quiet tone). With the old concat command swapped back in, the main test fails: "voice changed by up to 255 16-bit steps".
- Processing suite: 1240 passed, 5 skipped. Backend and frontend not touched, so their checks were not run.

**Other `anullsrc` uses checked:** the music gaps are safe (inside the filter graph the silence takes the music's format). Three others only ever make pure silence, which is exact in 8-bit. `build_clip_audio_track` has the same pattern but nothing calls it; left alone.

**Deploys:** merging deploys the dev renderer through CI (`deploy-dev.yml`). Prod gets it on the next release tag. Docs: `VIDEO_RENDERING.md` 2.5, `INDEX.md`, `progress.md`.

body:
Two problems with the photo camera, seen in a render of the tribute sample video:
1. **Portrait photos with a small face moved too fast.** The zoom itself was only 10%, but the wide view is a square from the middle of the photo and the face usually sits near the top, so the crop slid a long way while zooming: 4 to 7% of the frame per second, up to 27% of the frame over a 4 s photo.
2. **Photos where faces fill the frame barely moved** (zoom 1.00 to 1.03), because the close crop was never allowed tighter than the faces plus a 15% margin.

The founder compared test renders and picked "v1", which this implements in `zoom_crops`:
- The crop's centre moves at most 6% of the frame over a photo (`KB_MAX_TRAVEL = 0.06`).
- Every zoom is at least 6% (`KB_MIN_ZOOM = 1.06`), even if the close crop trims up to 20% off the face box (`KB_FACE_TRIM = 0.20`).
- Short Fast-pace photos keep their own, smaller zoom, and their travel limit shrinks in proportion, so a 1 s photo cannot slide 6% in one second.
- Pans, the choice of move, and the 10% zoom strength are unchanged.

**Checked against the approved render:** recomputed for all 23 photos of that video, the zoom matches v1 on every photo and the travel is the same or up to 0.2% of the frame per second gentler. The branch keeps the 6% limit where the test patch could exceed it (up to 7.5%) after clamping to the photo; a zoom into a corner can still move the centre up to 6.4%, as in the test patch.

**Tests:** processing suite 1320 passed, 5 skipped. 10 new tests in `test_camera.py` fail on the old code (full-frame zoom, small-face portrait, travel limit on 5 layouts, short Fast photos, no zoom means no movement). Two old tests were rewritten because the rules they pinned changed on purpose. Backend and frontend not touched.

**Deploys:** merging deploys the dev renderer through CI. Prod gets it on the next release tag. This PR and the voice static PR both edit `progress.md`, `INDEX.md` and `VIDEO_RENDERING.md`, so the second to merge will need those resolved. Docs: `VIDEO_RENDERING.md` 2.7 and 2.9.

body:
Found while testing a voice memory on dev. On a Premium project, "Invite to record" offered the Premium upgrade and made a link. Opening that link said "This project is not collecting voice memories right now". Voice memories are a Tribute-tier feature, but every route that hands out a recording link checked only the collaborators entitlement, which Premium has. So the app made links nobody could use.

## Fix
- **Backend:** one helper, `recordingLinkGate` (`backend/src/services/entitlements.js`), checks collaborators, then voice. It guards every route that makes a recording link:

  | Route | Before | Now |
  |---|---|---|
  | `POST /memories/:memoryId/share` | collaborators | collaborators + voice |
  | `POST /timeline-share` | collaborators | collaborators + voice |
  | `POST /share-codes`, `memory` or `timeline` scope | collaborators | collaborators + voice |
  | `POST /memories/pending` | **no tier gate at all** | collaborators + voice |

  A photos link (add-your-photos) still needs only collaborators. A Premium project gets a 400 with `{ requiredTier: 'tribute', source: 'voice' }`.
- **Frontend:** the timeline memory view's Invite button (`TimelineV2LightboxActions`) and the photo library's share-for-recording mode now call `gateVoice`, so the upgrade prompt offers Tribute.
- **Existing links:** a link already made on a Premium project starts working once the project moves to Tribute, because the check happens when the link is opened.

## Tests
- Eight new backend tests: three for the helper, five for the routes. With the handler change set aside, all five route tests fail; with it, they pass.
- The two timeline-link tests that passed on Premium (the bug) now run on Tribute.
- Backend: import check, lint (0 warnings), 2,937 tests. Frontend: lint (0 warnings), 1,762 tests, build.

## What merging deploys (from `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md`)
- `backend/**`: `deploy-dev.yml` deploys the dev backend.
- `frontend/**`: `deploy-frontend.yml` deploys the dev frontend.
- No renderer change.

Docs: `API.md` (tier rules per route), `FRONTEND.md` (tier gating), `INDEX.md`, `progress.md`.

body:
Create Video moves from the EC2 box to Google Cloud Run Jobs, one job execution per video. Finished videos go to a new Google Cloud Storage bucket. Every place that reads a video now handles both S3 and GCS; a record without the new `videoStorage` field still means S3, so all existing videos keep working. The renderer no longer calls Rekognition. Instead, upload analysis keeps its face data, and a one-time backfill fills in photos that lost it. EC2 stays as a fallback behind a per-stage switch (`RENDER_BACKEND`). After this merge dev renders on Cloud Run and prod stays on EC2 until the flip.

## What changed

| Area | Change |
|---|---|
| Renderer job | New `processing/Dockerfile` (FFmpeg from our own pinned image), `job_handler.py`, keyless AWS sign-in from Google (`cloud_credentials.py`), start claim so a video can't render twice, output to GCS (`VIDEO_OUTPUT_STORE`) |
| Dispatch | `renderDispatch.js`: Cloud Run job run with overrides, or SQS plus EC2; `setRenderBackend.js` flips a stage without a deploy |
| Sweep | Re-sends a lost Cloud Run dispatch once after 15 min (checks the execution first); starts a stopped EC2 box for a render queued over 10 min (#100) |
| Readers | `videoStorage.js`: owner play and download, share page, YouTube upload, delete and project delete for both stores |
| EC2 | Idle timer starts at finish and checks the queue once more; writes GCS too |
| Face data | Upload analysis asks Gemini for a fixed answer format; a bad or renamed box is repaired or dropped, never the whole photo's face data; `backfill_face_data.py` |
| Emails | Sends are awaited before the reply, SES calls have time limits (a "video ready" email was lost on dev today) |
| #151 | Four jobs that ran after the Lambda reply now finish first |
| CI | New `deploy-renderer-job.yml`; dev and prod deploy order is job, then EC2, then backend; a Backend Python job in `ci.yml` |
| Infra | `infra/iam/renderer-gcp/` with runbook G1-G14, bucket CORS and lifecycle, the failed-execution alert policy |
| Docs | VIDEO_RENDERING, INFRASTRUCTURE, DEPLOYMENT, ARCHITECTURE, OPERATIONS, DATA_MODEL, API, PIPELINES, CLAUDE.md, beta tracker bucket 19 (email branding) |

## What merging deploys (docs/DEPLOYMENT.md)

`deploy-dev.yml` only, in order: the `renderer-dev` Cloud Run job image, then the dev EC2 box, then the dev backend (`RENDER_BACKEND=cloudrun` on dev, `ec2` on prod). A failed job deploy stops the other two. No frontend and no Cloud Run video-processor deploy.

## Cloud state already in place (by hand, today)

Dev: `renderer-dev@`, `kindred-reels-renders-dev`, AWS role `kindred-renderer-gcp-dev-role`, the `renderer-dev` job with its four IAM bindings, and the failed-execution alert. Prod: `renderer-prod@`, `kindred-reels-renders-prod` and `kindred-renderer-gcp-prod-role`. The `renderer-prod` job (G14) must exist before the next release. Both federation proofs passed, including wrong-audience and cross-stage refusals.

## Tested on dev before this PR

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Comparison renders, EC2 vs Cloud Run (Colorado 720p with voice; Disney World with 29 clips, 3 sections and their own music, cover kept out; Outer Banks 2012 at 4K) | All pass: PSNR 41.3 to 47.2 dB average, worst 32.6+, SSIM 0.985+, audio byte-identical, same length to the frame |
| Render time vs EC2 | 1.28x and 1.44x at 720p; 4K 29 min 17 s vs 14 min 48 s, within the plan's 30 min |
| 4K memory | Peak 20.8 GiB of 32 |
| Start-up wait | 18 to 28 s once the image is cached (75 s on the first pull) |
| Kill test | Task killed at a 60 s limit, failed-execution metric recorded; alert email not yet confirmed |
| Face data backfill on dev | 238 of 238 filled, 2 photos left with no stored file |

Not yet tested: playback through the app and a YouTube upload of a GCS video (they need this backend), and the rollback drill. They come right after the merge.

## Follow-ups parked

#152 covers left in the timeline, #153 an import whose attempts all die before the cancel, #154 the "project full" message never shown. #146-#150 from the renderer move: copy old prod videos, keyless dispatch, sweep to 70 min, EC2 install.sh FFmpeg, decommission checklist.

allowed only 8, and a pool sized to the host fights itself for those 8 and

which is what the EC2 box and a laptop still get. The renderer and the
slideshow crossfade pools use it.

The idle clock started when a job was received and was checked straight after
the job, so any render longer than five minutes ended with the box stopping at
once, and a job queued during that render waited for the next start. The clock
now starts when a job finishes, a stop only follows an empty receive, and the
queue is asked once more (GetQueueAttributes, which the renderer roles already
allow) before the box stops. A failed check stops the box as before, so a
broken permission cannot keep it running.

sets up AWS credentials, logs the CPUs and memory the task got, runs the same

writes it to a 0600 file and points boto3's web identity provider at it before
any client exists, then rewrites the file at half the token's life. It does
nothing where AWS_ROLE_ARN is unset, so EC2 and laptops are unchanged.

commits.messageBody:
Review fixes T4-1 to T4-5 from the dispatch branch:

- The sweep re-sends a render to Cloud Run only when the record itself says
  renderBackend 'cloudrun'. A render whose dispatch was never recorded may be on the
  EC2 queue, so the stage switch alone no longer triggers a re-send. The claim's
  conditional write now also requires renderBackend = cloudrun.
- Before a re-send, the sweep asks the Cloud Run Admin API about the recorded
  execution (new getRenderExecution, same auth as runRenderJob). It re-sends only if
  that execution is gone (404) or has finished; one still pending or running, or one
  that cannot be looked up, is left alone. The replaced execution name is appended to
  previousRenderExecutions so its logs can still be found.
- setRenderBackend.js sends the RevisionId it read, so a deploy or another flip in
  between makes the write fail instead of writing back a stale environment.
- The Cloud Run run call (and the new lookup) has a 10 second deadline.
- The sweep starts the EC2 box at most once per queued render: a conditional
  renderEc2StartAt stamp on the VIDEO# row decides whether a render counts toward a
  start.

Tests cover each of these in renderDispatch, runRenderJob, sweepStuckVideos and
setRenderBackend.

produces what the prod EC2 box produces. processing/Dockerfile uses Amazon
Linux 2023 (pinned by digest) with the same font and Chromium packages,

and sha256. It runs as a non-root user.

Chromium screenshot, the Noto font path, the job entry point and the whole
processing test suite. The FFmpeg stage also runs both binaries at build time,
because a disk that filled mid-build left them cut short and crashing.

keyless AWS through federation, 8 render workers.

Review fixes T4-2 (job side) and T2-1 to T2-3:

- Start claim. db_client.claim_video_start writes the same start as
  update_video_started (processing, startedAt, sweep marker), but only if the record
  exists and was never started: no startedAt, and status 'queued' or the one 'failed'
  the sweep writes for a job that never started (still rendered, the same rule
  render_checks applies on EC2). job_handler claims before rendering. A lost claim,
  because another execution has it or the video is past queued, logs and exits 0
  without rendering. A claim that cannot be written exits 1 without rendering or
  marking anything, so the sweep's re-send gets another go. process_video_job takes

  a FINISHED one alone. cleanup_temp_files runs in a finally after the video is marked
  complete; a raise from it used to flip the video to failed and email the founder.
- A failed upload (a result with no s3_url) is no longer logged as "finished".
- The token refresh thread logs only while holding a lock that every fork takes first
  (os.register_at_fork). CPython resets the logging locks in a child, but not the
  lock inside buffered stderr, so a pool forked mid-log-line could hang.

test_cloud_credentials.py.

T1 review fix, in deploy-dev.yml and deploy-prod.yml. deploy-processing (the EC2
renderer) now waits for deploy-renderer-job. Before, the two ran side by side, so a
failed job deploy could leave the EC2 box already switched to GCS output while the job
and the backend were held back: the two renderers half-deployed.

Skipped still counts as a pass, the same guard deploy-backend has:
- A backend-only merge skips both renderer deploys and the backend still ships.
- A failed job deploy makes the EC2 deploy skip, and the backend stays held back
  because its guard still sees the job's failure.
- In prod, skip_processing is checked on deploy-processing directly as well, so it
  still skips both.

Checked by loading both files and reading back each job's needs and if.

commits.messageBody:
Second T1 review fix, approved by Dimitri. BtbN deletes autobuilds that are not
month-end, so a renderer build that downloaded the pinned tarball from GitHub would
break the day the release goes.

- processing/Dockerfile: the download stage is gone. The runtime stage copies
  /ffmpeg and /ffprobe from
  kindred-reels/ffmpeg:N-121938-g2456a39581@sha256:400bf13d...a1ed by digest, then
  runs both, so a binary cut short still fails the build. The BtbN URL and tarball
  sha256 stay as a comment saying where the copy came from.
- processing/deploy/ffmpeg/: the source of that image (FROM scratch, only the two
  binaries, the tarball checked against sha256 fec46f79...e87f) and a README with the
  exact build and push commands and how to move to another build.
- deploy-renderer-job.yml: signs in to Google and runs gcloud auth configure-docker
  BEFORE the build, because the build now pulls from Artifact Registry. Nothing is
  pushed until check_image.sh passes, as before. check_image.sh needed no change: it
  checks the running build name, not a download.
- infra/iam/renderer-gcp/RUNBOOK.md G6: configure Docker before the first build.

Not built or pushed here. The EC2 box's install.sh still installs BtbN latest; this
change is the container image only.

Merged-branch review fix 1. dispatchToCloudRun wrote renderBackend only after
runRenderJob succeeded. When the call threw (a 5xx, an auth error, the 10 s timeout)
the record carried no renderBackend, the sweep (which re-sends only a record that says
cloudrun) skipped it, and the video failed at 90 minutes. That is the main case the
re-send exists for.

Now renderBackend 'cloudrun' is recorded first, through the same conditional
recordRenderDispatch (nothing is written for a deleted video), and the execution name
after the call. The sweep re-sends such a record with no execution to look up. The
job's start claim stops a double render if the failed call did start an execution.

Tests: renderDispatch (order of the two writes, a failed call leaves the record marked,
the call still goes out when the first write fails, no second write without an
execution name) and sweepStuckVideos (a cloudrun record with no execution is re-sent).

commits.messageBody:
Merged-branch review fix 2. renderEc2StartAt was stamped before startVideoProcessor
ran. When the box was still stopping after the 60 s wait, or the start errored, the
render had used up its one start without a start happening, and no later sweep tried
again: exactly the #100 case the start exists for.

Now the sweep collects the queued EC2 renders that have no stamp, starts the box once,
and stamps each of them only when the result is 'started'. A box still stopping, one
already running, or a failed start stamps nothing, so the next sweep tries again.

Tests in sweepStuckVideos: the stamp comes after the start; nothing is stamped for
waiting, already running or a failed start; a render already stamped starts nothing;
one failed stamp does not stop the others.

Merged-branch review fix 3. job_handler's crash path marked the video failed and sent
the failure callback whenever it was not already finished. A crash before this
execution's start claim (the contents read, the output store check) could therefore
mark failed a video that another execution, the sweep's re-send or a retried run call,
had already started and was rendering.

run() now tracks whether this execution's claim succeeded. If it did not, and the
record read again (or, when that read fails, the first read) already has startedAt,
report_crash logs it and reports nothing; the job still exits 1. A crash after this
execution's own claim is reported as before.

Tests in test_job_handler.py: started elsewhere is left alone, a pre-claim crash with
no start is still reported, the first read is used when the re-read fails, and a crash
after the claim is reported even though startedAt is set.

commits.messageBody:
The analysis call had no response schema and the prompt only described the
face box corners in words, so the model often wrote `x` for `xmin` or mixed
0-1 fractions into 0-1000 boxes, and the boxes were dropped. The call now
sends response_mime_type application/json and response_json_schema: every
prompt field required, no other keys, the prompt's choices as enums, and
each face corner a required integer 0-1000. The schema covers every field
any code reads from geminiAnalysis, and a test searches the source to keep
it that way. google-genai 1.62.0 (the layer) and 2.28.0 both put it on the
Vertex request. Blocking, the fence strip and the retry are unchanged.

commits.messageBody:
The safety net behind the new answer format. normalize_face_box reads x or
left as xmin, y or top as ymin, right as xmax and bottom as ymax, only when
the real key is absent, and moves a corner written as a 0-1 fraction (not a
whole number, strictly between 0 and 1) to the 1000 scale, corner by corner,
since one real box mixed both scales. 0, 1 and anything above 1 stay. Repairs
and drops are counted and logged separately, clamping and dropping are kept.
The handler applies it once, so the stored geminiAnalysis.faces hold the same
boxes as faceData. Before this, a group photo whose boxes all said x lost
every face. Tested on the real dev boxes, including the 813a17 box that must
keep xmin 0.

commits.messageBody:
The fixed 0.05 pass mark was stricter than Gemini itself: the same photo sent
twice came back with noticeably different boxes. --compare now analyses each
sampled photo twice on one download and prints (a) the median distance from
the stored focus to the new one, (b) the median distance between the two new
runs, and (c) how many photos moved between faces and no faces and how the
face count shifted. It passes when (a) is at most (b) plus 0.02 and no photo
with faces came back with none only because its boxes were dropped. Repaired
and dropped box counts go in the CSV for both runs.

Review fixes for the face box parser. A corner of 1 (or 1.0) was always read
as 1 of 1000, so a box written in fractions that reached the right or bottom
edge lost its width and was dropped. Now the rest of the box decides: when
every other corner is a fraction (or 0 or 1) and at least one is a fraction,
1 is the edge and means 1000. Rounding to whole numbers moved into
usable_face_boxes, so a box with no area left after rounding is counted and
logged as dropped instead of quietly left out of the stored faces.

body:
Six fixes, bundled into one PR so they can ride in today's prod release. Each was built in its own branch, reviewed on its own, and the review fixes were applied before this merge.

| Fix | What changes for users |
|---|---|
| 200 MP photos | Photos from 200 MP phone cameras used to fail processing completely. Pillow's default limit refused anything over 179 MP, and 32 prod photos failed this way on 2026-10-04. The limit is now 268 MP, and big JPEGs are decoded at reduced size in the upload Lambda and the renderer. HEIC, PNG and WebP over 64 MP are refused with a clear message (#155). New `reprocessFailedPhotos.js` |
| One photo size limit | 50 MB everywhere: the upload screen, both upload-URL routes, both confirms and Google Photos imports. Before, uploads allowed 100 MB, the owner confirm 20 MB and the contributor confirm 100 MB, and a refused photo's file stayed in S3, up to three copies. A refused file is now deleted only if it is under its own photo's folder and no record uses it. A photo record can no longer overwrite an existing one. 408 and 429 now retry |
| #154 import message | When the project limit cuts a Google Photos import short, the user sees "42 of the 60 items you picked were added" and why. The contributor status route works now (it always 404ed before), and each contributor sees only their own import |
| Cancel a render | An in-progress video shows Cancel, styled like Download. It stops the Cloud Run execution, and the renderer skips the upload, so no orphan file is left. Checked live that a cancel counts as `cancelled`, not `failed`, so the alert does not fire. Also fixes the clipped red border on a row awaiting delete confirmation |
| Restoration copies | Restoration's full-size Google Cloud copies now go when their photo, project or account is deleted (a privacy leak). New `cleanupOrphanRestorationCopies.js` for the 110 left on dev |
| Email branding | All 13 emails move from black and blue to the app's brown and cream, on one shared layout, with a readable dark mode. The wording is unchanged, apart from the code sitting on the same line as its label. Previews: `cd backend && npm run email:preview`. Beta tracker bucket 19 |

## What merging deploys (docs/DEPLOYMENT.md)

- `deploy-dev.yml`: the `renderer-dev` job, then the dev EC2 box, then the dev backend.
- `deploy-frontend.yml`: the dev frontend, because `frontend/` changed.
- There are no `serverless.yml` changes and no cloud steps. The permissions the new code needs already exist.

## After it reaches prod (by hand, one yes each)

- Reprocess the 32 failed 200 MP photos with `reprocessFailedPhotos.js`.
- Run `cleanupOrphanRestorationCopies.js` on dev: a dry run first, then for real (#157).

## Checks

|---|---|
| Backend | 3,375 tests passed, lint clean |
| Frontend | 1,804 tests passed (run twice), lint clean, build OK |
| Processing | 1,465 tests passed |
| Backend Python | 204 tests passed |

- #156: a transparent PNG that needs rotating loses its analysis.

commits.messageBody:
Pillow's default decompression-bomb limit (179 MP) refused every photo
from the 200 MP mode of recent Samsung phones, so 32 prod photos failed
with no thumbnail and no analysis. The cap is now a deliberate 268 MP,
just under sharp's limit, so a real bomb is still refused at open.

A large JPEG that must be re-encoded (EXIF orientation, a rotation) is
decoded at the least reduction (1/2, 1/4, 1/8) that fits the Lambda's
1024 MB; measured on a 200 MP photo this drops the peak from 1.7 GB to
0.7 GB. HEIC, PNG and WebP over 64 MP cannot be decoded at reduced scale
and are refused with a clear sentence instead of running out of memory.
Gemini gets the 1,536 px analysis copy when a photo is over 6 MB or
64 MP, since Vertex AI takes at most 7 MB of inline image data. The face
backfill prepares images the same way.

Every Image.open in the renderer hit Pillow's default 179 MP limit, so a
200 MP photo could not be drawn, and the header read that picks a pan's

Nothing is rendered above 4K, so a downloaded photo over 5120 px on the

for JPEG. Every later reader sees the small file: the Ken Burns loaders,
ffprobe's check, the pan check and the title cards' page for Chromium.
The tests decode a real 200 MP JPEG in a separate process, since
conftest mocks Pillow for the rest of the suite.

body:
The dev deploy of #255 stopped at the renderer image check. Four new tests in `processing/tests/test_cancelled_render.py` let the render's download step create a relative `./temp` folder, and `check_image.sh` mounts the checkout read-only. They passed on the laptop and in CI, where the folder is writable. So the frontend deployed, but the renderer job, the EC2 box and the backend did not.

The fix runs those tests from `tmp_path` and points `TEMP_DIR` into it. Test-only; no product code changes.

Checked the same way the deploy does: the image built from this branch, with the full processing suite run inside it and the checkout mounted read-only. 1465 passed, 5 skipped.

Merging reruns `deploy-dev.yml`: renderer job, then EC2, then backend, which finishes the #255 deploy.
